14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The latitudinal slope of alpha diversity will flatten over time and its magnitude will decline toward zero.

Under Hubbell’s unified neutral theory local alpha diversity is set by the balance of ecological drift, speciation and immigration into a local community from the regional metacommunity. The 12 sites span a classic latitudinal gradient in regional species pools and in effective immigration, so alpha diversity rises toward the equator simply because the equatorial metacommunity is larger and immigration limitation is weaker at low latitudes.

The European invader is now a high-dispersal member of the metacommunity that is present at every site from Ottawa to Tena. Because neutral theory treats species as ecologically equivalent, its fate is governed by drift and the immigration–extinction balance rather than by a competitive advantage. Once it is established it contributes a persistent source of propagules to the entire network. Immigration limitation is strongest at high-latitude sites where regional richness and propagule rain are naturally low. A widespread, highly mobile immigrant therefore raises local alpha diversity proportionally more in the north than in the already species saturated equatorial sites.

In effect the invader raises the effective regional theta and supplies a homogenising dispersal flux along the latitudinal axis. Beta diversity declines and the alpha values converge across the transect as the northern communities are ‘filled in’ faster than the southern ones. Re-measurement in the future should therefore show a shallower, less steep increase of insect alpha diversity toward the equator, with the slope progressively flattening as the gradient is eroded by neutral dispersal homogenisation.

17.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The latitudinal increase in alpha diversity is going to erode and the slope will flatten, essentially be attenuated toward zero.

Under Hubbell’s unified neutral theory local alpha richness at a site is a stochastic sample of the metacommunity set by community size, per capita speciation ν and per capita immigration m, not by species-specific competitive superiority. Once the European invader is present in the whole Americas it becomes a permanent, highly dispersive member of the metacommunity and is incorporated into the regional species abundance distribution on neutral terms. 

In practice that means effective immigration is raised and the regional pool is increasingly homogenised across the 12 localities. Sites that were previously limited by low immigration from a species-rich tropical source, i.e. the high-latitude sites, experience a relatively larger neutral boost in the number of individuals and species they can maintain from the now pan-American pool, while the already species saturated equatorial sites gain little and lose local species to drift as the invader joins the zero-sum lottery. 

That is the classic neutral expectation of biotic homogenisation: local communities converge toward the same neutral expectation set by the common metacommunity size and dispersal regime. The tropical excess generated by a higher tropical ν is progressively diluted by pan-continental dispersal and neutral drift, so the alpha diversity vs. latitude relationship loses its steepness. In the long term the observed north-south gradient in alpha diversity is flattened, with the slope decreasing in magnitude and approaching a much more even, low-gradient pattern across Tena to Ottawa.

16.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Under Hubbell’s neutral model local alpha diversity is essentially a random sample of the regional metacommunity, with the latitudinal increase in alpha richness reflecting a larger regional species pool / higher metacommunity theta towards the equator rather than any deterministic niche advantage. An introduced, highly dispersive species that establishes everywhere is just another ecologically equivalent draw from that metacommunity. 

Because it is able to drift to high relative abundance across the whole transect, it will displace native species proportionally to its abundance. The absolute number of native species displaced is therefore much larger where the regional pool and the expected local richness are largest. Tropical sites such as Tena, Cali and Barro Colorado Island start with a much larger alpha richness than Ottawa or State College, so the same neutral drift-induced increase in the frequency of the invader removes more species in absolute terms near the equator than at temperate sites. The temperate trough is eroded only modestly in absolute terms while the tropical peak is eroded strongly.

That asymmetric absolute loss attenuates the equator-to-pole increase in local richness, i.e. the latitudinal alpha diversity gradient is flattened. In the long neutral equilibrium the slope of alpha diversity vs latitude becomes less positive, with the tropical-temperate contrast reduced relative to the pre-invasion baseline, even though the rank order of sites is preserved.

21.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Under Hubbell’s neutral framework the latitudinal gradient in local alpha diversity is essentially an immigration-drift equilibrium set by metacommunity size and dispersal. The invader is now a cosmopolitan member of the New World metacommunity and, by neutrality, it is ecologically equivalent to the natives it replaces. That means its incorporation into local communities is governed by drift and immigration, not by superior competitive ability.

Immigration limitation is strongest at the high-latitude, low-diversity ends of the transect where local communities are smaller and drift is more effective at losing rare species. Adding a highly dispersive, now everywhere-present species to the regional pool therefore raises the expected local richness and, more importantly, the expected local abundance of a given metacommunity frequency, disproportionately in those immigration-limited sites. In the equatorial sites the local assemblage is already saturated with respect to the neutral immigration-drift balance and the species pool is large, so the proportional gain in alpha diversity from the new widespread neutral species is diluted.

The net effect is an increase in alpha diversity that is larger at high latitudes than at low latitudes, i.e., an upward shift that is steeper towards the pole. The latitudinal alpha diversity increase with decreasing latitude therefore becomes shallower, the slope of alpha diversity vs latitude flattens toward zero and the equator-to-pole contrast is reduced over time.

15.text:
Under Hubbell the latitudinal pattern of alpha diversity is not a niche 
pattern at all.  In the zero sum multinomial limit

* E[Slocal|J,theta] ~ f(theta ,J) ,      theta = 2Jm nu ,

where theta is the fundamental biodiversity number of the metacommunity
that feeds the local community, J is local community size and nu is the
per capita speciation rate.  The classic latitudinal increase in alpha
is the neutral emergent consequence of a latitudinal increase in the
regional theta, i.e. a larger regional species pool and, in the usual
formulation, a larger per capita speciation rate in the tropics, together
with dispersal limitation and zero sum demographic drift.  Species
identity and species specific competitive superiority are not parameters
of the model.

In neutral terms the European invader is just one more ecologically
equivalent draw from the regional pool.  It cannot be allowed a
persistent competitive advantage and its long term fate is that of any
other species, namely stochastic increase / decrease by demographic drift,
immigration and speciation/extinction.  Once the invader is present in
the continent-wide metacommunity it is present, at neutral expectation,
in every local community that is connected to the metacommunity and it
contributes the same, ecologically equivalent, increment to the zero sum
species abundance distribution everywhere. The competitive story that
is invoked in niche theory is therefore neutrally irrelevant in the
long run.

In the long run the system relaxes to the neutral equilibrium set by
regional theta, Jm and m and the latitudinal increase in alpha diversity
is maintained by the latitudinal increase in regional theta / speciation
and by drift/dispersal, not by the identity or competitive ability of any
single species.  Any transient loss of natives that is seen immediately
after the invasion is proportional to local richness and is swamped by
neutral drift/immigration so that the neutral expectation for the
alpha vs latitude relationship is recovered.  In the verbal shorthand
which is normally used this is described as neutral homogenisation:
the widespread common species increases mixing among sites, beta
diversity is reduced and the alpha diversity gradient is damped and in
the strict dispersal unlimited neutral limit is homogenised toward the
regional mean.  The persistent, competition driven steepening or
flattening of the alpha gradient that niche theory would predict does not
exist under neutrality; the gradient is a neutral emergent property and
in the ultimate neutral equilibrium it is essentially unchanged and is
set by speciation, drift and dispersal, not by the invasive’s ability to
out-compete natives.  That is the usual statement that the competitive
impact is transient and ultimately neutralised.

19.text:
Under the Unified Neutral Theory of Biodiversity and Biogeography all co-occurring species are ecologically equivalent and local community composition is the outcome of stochastic birth-death-immigration-speciation drift in a metacommunity. 

The classic latitudinal increase in local alpha diversity that you are seeing with
Tena > … > Ottawa is the neutral expectation for a set of communities sampled from
a metacommunity whose size, speciation rate and net immigration increase towards
the low latitudes. The putative ‘ability to out-compete many natives’ of the
European insect is therefore irrelevant for long-term community structure under
UNT. Competition in the sense of deterministic competitive exclusion does not
exist, it is replaced by neutral drift and regional dispersal.

At demographic equilibrium the invader becomes just one more neutrally sampled
species in the American insect metacommunity of the trophic level in question. In
the limit it is present in every local community and is sampled locally in
proportion to its metacommunity relative abundance. The net long-term effect
is therefore essentially a neutral addition of a widespread species to the
regional pool,

Smeta → Smeta +1

and a neutrally sampled addition to every local community,

Sα,i(t→∞) ≈ Sα,i0 + ΔSneut,i,

with ΔSneut,i ≃ 1 for all i. In absolute terms the local richness is
raised by essentially the same amount everywhere, so the latitudinal
α-diversity profile is translated up but is not systematically reshaped by
competition. The equatorial > tropical > temperate increase in alpha diversity,
i.e. the positive equatorial slope, is maintained by neutral drift, immigration
and the underlying gradient in metacommunity size/speciation. In proportional
terms the increment is a little larger at high-latitude, species-poor sites
because of the saturating neutral species–area/immigration relationship, so in
practice the gradient is essentially conserved and at most very slightly
flattened by the added cosmopolitan neutral element. There is no persistent
competition-driven loss of native alpha diversity and no long-term change in
the neutrally generated latitudinal slope produced by the invasion.

20.text:
Under strict neutrality there is no niche based competitive superiority and
hence no niche based competitive displacement.  In the unified neutral
theory all species in the metacommunity are ecologically equivalent and
local relative abundances are generated by stochastic ecological drift,
speciation at rate ν and dispersal–immigration at rate m.  The expected
local species richness in the zero-sum multinomial limit is a function of
the local community size J, the metacommunity parameter θ = 2νJ_M and the
immigration parameter m and in the limit m→0 it is set by the regional
speciation–immigration balance.  The classic equatorward increase in
alpha richness is then the neutral expectation of a higher long term
regional species pool θ in the tropics, i.e. effectively a higher net
speciation rate in the low latitude metacommunity, not the outcome of
local competitive exclusion.

In particular a species that is present in the metacommunity is just
another neutrally equivalent species.  The introduction of one
cosmopolitan neutral species adds essentially the same expected
increment to the local species pool at every locality in which it can
immigrate.  On average it is a uniform +1 to local richness when it is
present, or, in a zero sum formulation, a neutrally fluctuating
replacement, so that the between site pattern in Sα is not altered in a
latitudinally structured way. There is no neutral mechanism by which the
invasive can systematically out compete and remove more natives at low
latitude than at high latitude, or vice versa.  The latitudinal alpha
gradient therefore persists under neutrality.

In practice that means the biologically meaningful competition driven
change that the researchers are interested in is null under Hubbell.
Formally the expected alpha richness is increased essentially uniformly
by the cosmopolitan invader so that Sα,i(t→∞)=Sα,i(0)+Δ with Δ≈1
everywhere, i.e. the intercept of the Sα–latitude relationship is
raised a trivial amount and the slope dSα/d latitude remains positive
and essentially unchanged.  If the uniform addition is removed the
often quoted neutral statement is that a truly metacommunity-wide
disperser homogenises local composition and increases immigration–
mediated rescue at the species-poor high latitude end so that the
observed alpha gradient is slightly attenuated/flattened with time,
tending towards greater among-site homogenisation.  The flattening is a
dispersal homogenisation effect, not a competition driven loss of
natives, and in the strict neutral limit the equilibrium latitudinal
alpha gradient set by the latitudinal variation in θ and m is retained.

18.text:
Under a neutral metacommunity the fitness differences that are invoked in
the niche picture are by definition absent.

In the Hubbell zero-sum multinomial the local community at a site is just
a sample without replacement of a common regional pool.  Local  alpha
richness is

Sα ≈ f(θ , J , m )

where θ = 2Jmν is the fundamental biodiversity number of the
metacommunity, J the local community size and m the per capita
immigration probability.  Speciation ν, community size J and the
immigration / dispersal regime set the regional γ diversity and the
expected Sα at a site.  Ecological equivalence means that a species that
is introduced from Europe has no intrinsic competitive superiority to
native species in the same trophic level. Its fate in a local community
is that of any other species: increase or decrease in abundance
and the possibility of local extinction is set by demographic stochasticity
and immigration, not by deterministic competitive exclusion.

Hence the niche expectation that a superior invader will selectively
remove more native species in the species rich tropics and therefore
flatten the latitudinal alpha gradient is a niche prediction.  In the
strict neutral limit the invader is just one more ecologically equivalent
species drawn from the metacommunity.  On average it replaces a random
native species in the zero-sum lottery, so that to first order there is
no latitudinally biased loss of Sα.  In particular the classical
latitudinal alpha gradient, Sα↑ toward the equator, is the neutral
drift / immigration / speciation gradient

Sα,lat ≈ θlat ln[1+J/θlat]

and it is maintained by the latitudinal increase in ν and/or J and by
the metacommunity sampling effect, not by local competitive
displacement.  Ecologically, over ecological time scales the alpha
diversity–latitude relationship therefore stays essentially as it is
observed now, i.e. a positive slope Sα vs latitude with no systematic
neutrally-driven flattening produced by competitive exclusion.

In the limit of very high effective dispersal the widespread invader
makes the regional pool more homogeneous, β-diversity falls and the
local communities become more similar to the metacommunity mean.
That is the usual neutral homogenisation effect: any increase in
effective m raises Sα most in historically species poor, high-latitude
sites where Sα is far from the regional saturation curve and raises it
least in the species saturated tropics.  The net neutral effect is
therefore a weak tendency for the inter-site variance in Sα to shrink
and for the observed alpha-vs-latitude slope to weaken / flatten toward
the common metacommunity expectation, and in the idealised infinite
mixing limit the slope would tend to zero.  The important neutral
point is that the flattening, if it occurs, is a dispersal/drift
homogenisation effect, not a competitive displacement of tropical
natives by a superior invader.  In the conventional strict zero-sum
neutral formulation the slope is effectively conserved. ∎

public_text.5:
The latitudinal gradient in mean alpha will be eroded over time so the slope flattens toward zero.

Under Hubbell’s unified neutral theory local communities are not structured by deterministic niche superiority and competitive displacement is not a persistent force. All species in the trophic level are functionally equivalent, so the invasive is just a new neutral draw into the regional metacommunity that now spans the whole North and South American range. Local alpha at a site is set by the neutral balance of immigration m from the metacommunity, community size J and the fundamental biodiversity number θ.

Initially the invasion can look like deterministic exclusion and alpha will dip most where local richness is highest, i.e. near the equator, and the dip will be transient. Once the invasive is fully integrated into the metacommunity, drift and dispersal will re-randomize relative abundances and the expected species abundance distribution and mean local richness for a given m and J is recovered. Because the invasive is now present at high frequency across the entire latitudinal transect, it raises the regional frequency of one taxon everywhere and reduces the effective regional pool of distinct neutral draws that can immigrate to any site.

That metacommunity-wide homogenization acts to push local alpha toward a common neutral expectation set by dispersal limitation rather than by the pre-invasion latitudinal species pool. The transient competitive signal is swamped by stochastic turnover and the historical differences in mean alpha driven by geography are progressively dampened. In practice the observed diversity-vs-latitude relationship becomes shallower with time and, at neutral equilibrium, the systematic increase in alpha towards the equator is lost and the slope tends toward flat.
public_text.2:
The latitudinal increase in alpha diversity will weaken and the slope will flatten toward zero over time.

Under Hubbell’s unified neutral theory local alpha diversity is an equilibrium outcome of local community size, per-capita birth-death-immigration rates and the size of the regional metacommunity pool, with all species ecologically equivalent. The equatorial sites in the set sit in a larger, more productive metacommunity with a higher fundamental biodiversity number and therefore a higher immigration supply and a higher neutral expectation for Sα than the high-latitude sites. That is why the present data show a positive diversity-latitude relationship.

Once the European invader is present everywhere from Ottawa to Tena it becomes a ubiquitous member of the metacommunity and a constant source of propagules to every local community. In neutral dynamics that is functionally an increase in regional connectivity and a homogenizing immigration pressure. The low-latitude communities, which under neutrality are already close to saturation for a given J because of a large θ, will experience the invader mainly as replacement via drift and as additional mean abundance that displaces rare natives. The high-latitude communities, with a smaller θ and more empty niche space in neutral terms, can accommodate the widespread propagule pool with a proportionally larger relative increase in local species richness. In other words, neutral drift and immigration from a now pan-American pool act to raise the floor of alpha diversity at the north and raise the ceiling less at the tropics.

The net effect is convergence of Sα across the 12 sites: the tropical sites lose a larger absolute number of rare species to stochastic turnover in the face of a constant invader, while the temperate/boreal sites gain. The latitudinal gradient is therefore eroded. The equilibrium slope of mean alpha diversity versus latitude is reduced in magnitude and, on the time scale on which the metacommunity re-equilibrates, tends toward homogenization.
public_text.7:
Under Hubbell the latitudinal pattern in alpha diversity is not a niche-driven equilibrium but a sampling outcome from a regional metacommunity governed by speciation, dispersal and drift. Local richness is expected to track the size and connectivity of the regional species pool and the immigration rate m, with demographic stochasticity driving communities toward a common neutral expectation when dispersal is strong.

A pan-American invader that reaches all 12 sites effectively raises long-distance connectivity and adds a single, very widespread abundant type to the regional pool. Because neutral dynamics are purely stochastic, the invader will be incorporated into the regional theta and will be sampled at high frequency in every local community. That sampling acts to homogenize local communities across the gradient: high-diversity low-latitude sites lose a larger absolute number of rare natives to drift and to the increased regional dominance of the widespread type, whereas low-diversity high-latitude sites are pushed upward toward the regional mean by immigration.

In practice the alpha diversity – latitude relationship that is initially seen is a transient biogeographic signal. With continued neutral mixing the local communities converge toward the same expectation set by the now more connected, invader-mediated metacommunity. The net effect is a progressive weakening of the latitudinal slope, i.e. a flattening of the diversity gradient with time, toward effectively zero difference between equatorial and temperate sites at neutral equilibrium.
public_text.4:
Under Hubbell the niche differences that are used to talk about “out-compete’’ do not exist.  In the UNTB all species in the trophic level are ecologically equivalent and local assemblages are samples, with immigration, of a regional metacommunity whose
equilibrium is set by demographic drift, speciation and the dispersal rate m,
i.e. by the fundamental biodiversity number θ =2Jmν .  Local α at
equilibrium is

Sα ≈ θ ln[1+mJ/(θ(1-m))]

to first order and is therefore a function of local community size J and
of the regional immigration pool, not of local adaptation.  In a
species-rich metacommunity the zero-sum multinomial gives a common
species abundance distribution for every local community that is
connected to that pool.

A species that is really everywhere in the Americas is, in neutral
terms, a very high m species. It raises the effective connectivity of the
metacommunity and acts as a metacommunity-wide source. The stochastic
replacements that follow are ecological drift and immigration and not
directional competitive displacement.  The net neutral effect is a
homogenising one: local communities are increasingly drawn from the
same regional pool and the differences in local immigration historically
associated with the productivity / speciation gradient toward the equator
are swamped by the high-dispersal, essentially pan-American source.

In practice that is a decrease in β-diversity along the transect and an
increase in the sharing of the same set of common species, the
introduced one in particular, at all latitudes. In the long term α at a
high-latitude site, which is immigration limited and starts with a small
Sα, is lifted toward the regional value, while α at the low-latitude,
historically high-diversity sites is drawn down by drift/replacement with
the widespread invader.  The positive equator to pole gradient in
α-diversity is therefore eroded. 

In the neutral limit the gradient is removed and the transect tends to a
flat, essentially m and J determined, mean α, i.e. the slope dSα/dlatitude
goes to zero, a shallower and ultimately vanishing latitudinal α
gradient. That is the neutral homogenisation prediction; in the language
of competition the “out-competition’’ story is neutrally irrelevant, the
observed change is drift + immigration homogenisation.
public_text.3:
Under Hubbell the species that make up the local trophic guild are
ecologically interchangeable. Local species richness is a sampling
property of a regional metacommunity

* Sα ≈ f(Jl , θm , m) ,   θm = 2Jm ν

with a metacommunity parameter θm = 2Jmν set by regional
abundance, speciation ν and , in the simplest formulation, a common
immigration probability m, and it is the between-site differences in
Jl, m and the regional speciation / area that generate a latitudinal
α-gradient.  With ecological equivalence there is no deterministic
niche competitive superiority that can be ascribed to the European
insect. In the formal neutral limit the “potential to out-compete many
natives’’ is a null expectation. Local assemblages are therefore
continually re-sampled from the same regional species pool by
ecological drift and dispersal, and the only long term signal is the
neutral sampling one set by J l , m and θm.

In particular an essentially cosmopolitan addition to the metacommunity
makes the regional pool better mixed.  To a first approximation the
invasion adds one essentially ubiquitous metacommunity species to the
pool and, by increasing effective connectivity, it increases β
homogenisation. The neutral local abundance distribution is then
drawn from a pool in which the same widespread common species is
present at essentially the same relative frequency at Tena, Ecuador as
at Ottawa, Canada.  The proportional increase in Sα produced by the
addition of a common widespread species is greatest where Sα is
initially low and the effective sampling variance due to drift is
greatest.  In the long neutral limit the among-site variance in α
richness generated by different local sampling of the same metacommunity
is therefore eroded.

That is the familiar neutral homogenisation result.  Formally the
invasion has no deterministic competitive effect on Sα, so the
competition-driven expectation of a steeper loss of diversity towards
the equator is not realised in the neutral model.  In practice the
neutral expectation is a weakening of the observed latitudinal α
gradient, a flattening of the richness ~ latitude relationship and,
in the strict, well mixed, equilibrium neutral limit, Sα → the same
neutral sampling expectation at all sites, i.e. the slope of α
diversity against latitude tends to zero.  In the idealised strict
neutral statement the latitudinal α-gradient that is set by regional
speciation/area and dispersal is retained and the putative competitive
decline of native richness is null. ∎
public_text.1:
In Hubbell's UNTB the species in the metacommunity are ecologically
equivalent. Birth, death, immigration and speciation occur at the same
per capita rates for all species and the only force that can structure
local abundances is demographic stochasticity/drift coupled to dispersal
limitation and the regional speciation rate. A species that has been
introduced from Europe is therefore, in the neutral limit, just another
member of the regional species pool.  It has no intrinsic per capita
competitive advantage and it cannot systematically drive resident species
out of local communities by niche displacement.

In the neutral limit the equilibrium local alpha richness at a site is a
function of local community size J, the immigration rate m and the
species-abundance distribution of the metacommunity in which the site is
embedded.  In the classic Hubbell formulation the metacommunity species
abundance distribution, and hence the regional gamma richness, is set
by the balance of speciation $\nu$ and drift.  With the usual
geographical implementation $\nu$, and therefore $\gamma$, is larger in
the tropics, so that the neutral expectation is an increasing alpha
richness towards the equator

$ S_{\alpha}( \lambda)\approx f\!\left[J,m(\lambda),\theta(\lambda)\right] $

with $\theta$ the fundamental biodiversity number which is itself a
function of regional speciation. The latitudinal alpha gradient is
therefore a neutral speciation/dispersal gradient, not a gradient in
local competitive ability.

Putting a single, highly dispersive species into the American
metacommunity therefore does not change the neutral mechanisms that
generate the alpha-latitude relationship. At long term equilibrium the
invader will have an equilibrium metacommunity relative abundance
$\widehat{x}_{inv}$ and an occupancy that tends to one because of the
assumed rapid range-wide dispersal.  Locally

$S_{\alpha}^{t\to\infty}\approx S_{\alpha}^{0}+p_{occ}\,,
\qquad p_{occ}\approx \widehat{x}_{inv}  $

i.e. to first order the whole alpha vs latitude curve is translated up
in parallel by the essentially constant occupancy of a cosmopolitan
species. In absolute terms the increase $\Delta S_{\alpha}$ towards the
equator is preserved,

$\Delta S_{\alpha}^{tropics-north}^{t\to\infty}\approx
\Delta S_{\alpha}^{tropics-north}^{0},$

so that the qualitative neutral latitudinal diversity gradient is
maintained. In proportional terms the addition of a ubiquitous species
raises species poor northern sites by a larger fraction than the
species rich equatorial sites, so that the relative slope
$ d\ln S_{\alpha}/d{\rm lat}$ is weakly homogenised/flattened. That is
the neutral analogue of “no competitive displacement”: there is no
niche theory driven loss of native alpha richness and no neutral
theory driven collapse of the gradient, the increase of site level
alpha diversity towards the equator persists and, to a very good
approximation, the alpha-latitude relationship is simply shifted upward
in parallel.  If the slope is reported in proportional terms the
usual textbook statement is that the gradient is homogenised and the
apparent slope of alpha diversity with latitude is reduced, i.e. the
American insect assemblages become more similar in alpha richness with
no systematic competitive decline of the tropical sites.  This is the
neutral null to the niche expectation of a tropical loss of diversity
by competitive exclusion.
public_text.6:
Under a strict Hubbell neutral world species are ecologically equivalent. 
Per capita birth, death and immigration rates are the same for the
invasive and for any native that it is in the same trophic guild with so
that any supposed difference in competitive ability is, by construction,
irrelevant for the dynamics of the community. The latitudinal change
in local alpha richness that is seen in the 12 sites is in the neutral
picture the emergent consequence of neutral drift, immigration–emigration
balance and of a regional  θ=2Jmν , i.e. of metacommunity size and of
the background speciation rate, not of a latitudinal change in
interspecific competition. In particular the neutral expectation for a
local community of J individuals drawn from a metacommunity with basic
biodiversity number θ is

S(J|θ,m) ≈ θ·[ ψ(J+θ) - ψ(1+θ)] + …,

so that mean local richness increases with regional θ and with local
J and is a monotone, saturating function of θ. The tropics have in the
Hubbell picture a larger effective metacommunity size and therefore a
larger regional θ and a larger equilibrium local S than the temperate
sites. That is the neutral latitudinal alpha gradient.

Adding a cosmopolitan invader to the Americas is in the neutral picture
just the addition of one more neutral draw to the regional pool.  In the
limit of long time and free dispersal the invader will be present in
every local community with a frequency set by neutral drift and by its
relative abundance in the metacommunity, exactly like any other species.
There is no neutral mechanism by which a species can be systematically
lost from the species-rich tropical sites more than from the species-poor
temperate sites.  The invasion therefore cannot generate a
competition-mediated steepening of the alpha vs. latitude relationship.
The directional increase of mean alpha richness towards the equator
persists as the neutral prediction and the invasion does not produce a
competitive disruption of the slope.

In the usual formalisation this shows up as a diminishing marginal
return of an increase in regional θ : ∂S/∂θ>0 but ∂²S/∂θ²<0.  The
addition of a ubiquitous neutral species therefore raises S everywhere
but the fractional increase is larger where S is initially small.  In
practice the gradient is therefore essentially conserved in sign – alpha
richness is still higher towards the Equator – and the only neutral
effect of a truly cosmopolitan neutral invader is a very weak
flattening/homogenisation of the alpha vs. latitude relationship
rather than the competition driven loss of tropical diversity that is
normally expected under niche theory.  In the strict zero-sum neutral
limit this is usually phrased as the slope being unchanged by the
invasion: the latitudinal alpha gradient remains the neutral
speciation–drift–dispersal gradient and competitive displacement has no
neutral effect on it. ∎
public_text.9:
The latitudinal increase in alpha diversity will be eroded and the slope will flatten, eventually trending toward a much shallower increase with latitude under a neutral expectation.

Under Hubbell’s UNTB local richness at equilibrium is set by the size of the local community J, the metacommunity size Jm and the effective immigration rate m, with the regional species pool itself being the product of speciation and drift. The classic equator-to-pole rise in observed alpha is produced in the neutral scheme by a larger regional pool and higher effective turnover toward the equator, not by in situ niche differences.

A species that achieves essentially pan-American occupancy in this trophic level becomes a universally present, high-frequency element in the metacommunity. In neutral terms it raises the baseline probability of occurrence everywhere and participates in the same ecological drift that governs the loss of rare natives. Because drift loss of rare species is a function of local richness, the demographic draw-down is largest where local species richness is initially largest. 

Equatorial sites like Tena, Cali and Barro Colorado start with a much larger local SAR than Ottawa or State College. The invader’s increased mean abundance therefore removes rare natives, in expectation, from a larger standing pool at low latitudes than at high latitudes. The high-latitude sites have so few species to begin with that the same pan-continental propagule pressure cannot depress richness as much in absolute terms.

Over long neutral timescales that differential loss in expectation converges local richness across the transect. The metacommunity remains dominated by drift and by the now homogenized, continent-wide presence of one abundant taxon, so the latitudinal signal in alpha that is normally generated by a steeper regional pool toward the equator is dampened. In practice the alpha vs. latitude relationship stays positive but becomes markedly shallower, i.e. the slope in diversity per degree latitude declines in magnitude as the invasive spreads via neutral dispersal and drift.
public_text.8:
Under a strict Hubbell neutral world species are ecologically equivalent and
local assemblages are samples of a single, globally mixing metacommunity
subject to zero-sum ecological drift, dispersal limitation,  speciation
and extinction.  The equilibrium number of species that a local sample of
J individuals can harbour is

Sα ≈ θ* [ ψ(1+J/θ*) - ψ(1+1/θ*) ] ,   θ* = 2Jmν/(1-m) ,

essentially a function of local community size J, the per capita
immigration probability m and the metacommunity parameter ν the
speciation rate.  The latitudinal alpha-richness – latitude relationship
that you are seeing now is the neutral realisation of the geographical
variation in the regional species pool θ, i.e. of a higher per-capita
speciation ν near the equator and of the decreasing immigration
supply  m with increasing distance from the tropical species pool.  It
is not a relationship generated by species-specific niche differences
or by species-specific competitive superiority.

In that neutral world the European insect is just one more ecologically
equivalent particle that is now part of the American metacommunity. Its
per capita birth, death and dispersal rates are by definition identical
to those of the native insects and the classic “the invasive can
out-compete natives’’ statement is operationally empty.  The species
will be incorporated into the metacommunity by neutral drift and will
subsequently be present in the local samples with a frequency that is
on average proportional to its metacommunity relative abundance. 
On the long time scale the zero-sum replacement that the introduction
produces is random with respect to latitude. In particular there is no
neutrally generated, latitudinally biased loss of native species.  The
addition of the cosmopolitan species therefore produces at most a
roughly latitude independent upward shift in the expected Sα at every
sample, Sα→ Sα + ΔSα, with ΔSα ≈ the neutral occupancy of the new
particle, so that the first order slope

 d Sα / d Lat

set by the neutral speciation–dispersal gradient is maintained.  In
other words the competition-driven flattening of the gradient that would
be expected under a niche/competitive displacement model does not occur
under neutrality.

In the idealised panmictic limit m→1 the neutral model predicts
complete homogenisation of the local samples with the metacommunity and
the geographical gradient in alpha richness is formally erased, the
slope going to zero.  That is the usual statement that neutral drift plus
ubiquitous dispersal homogenises communities.  In the more realistic
Hubbell formulation with a latitude dependent speciation rate ν(lat) the
speciation driven gradient in θ* persists, so in practice the
observed pole-to-equator increase in insect α-diversity persists and
the invasion does not generate a latitudinally structured decrease in
α-diversity.  The slope is therefore not flattened by competitive
displacement; the invasion is neutrally neutral and, apart from a
common, essentially latitude-independent increment in richness due to
the new neutral particle, the alpha–latitude relationship remains the
one set by neutral speciation and dispersal.  This is often phrased as
the neutral prediction that the latitudinal gradient in α-diversity is
maintained and the invasion does not produce the competition-mediated
steepening/flattening that a niche model would predict.
public_text.10:
In Hubbell's UNTB every species is ecologically equivalent and local
composition is the outcome of stochastic birth-death, speciation ν and
immigration m from a metacommunity of size Jm.  Local alpha richness
is

 Sα ≈ θ ln[1+Jm/θ] ,    θ=2νJm

and is set by the size of the local community, the regional θ and the
immigration rate m, not by differences in per capita competitive
ability.  Latitudinal differences in Sα in the neutral picture are
therefore not a niche filtering/competition effect but the emergent
consequence of a latitudinally varying speciation-immigration-drift
balance – essentially a species-area / metacommunity size effect – with
the metacommunity Sγ itself being higher towards the equator because of
higher historical speciation.

Hence a species that can ‘out-compete’ natives in a niche sense has no
systematic neutral effect.  In the long term the European insect is just
another neutral species that becomes part of the metacommunity pool and
is incorporated into every local community by the same zero sum
multinomial sampling that governs all the other species.  In the
zero-sum limit it can only replace individuals of the resident species
at random.  Its continental scale dispersal makes it a ubiquitously
immigrating species, so it is added, in expectation, to every local
community.  Adding a constant ubiquitous species,
Sα(lat) → Sα(lat)+c, does not change the latitudinal derivative
dSα/dlat, and the loss of resident individuals it causes is random with
respect to latitude.

In practice the addition of a ubiquitous taxon raises local richness
more in proportion at the low-diversity, low-m northern end of the
transect than at the high-diversity equatorial end and the transient
niche-driven amplification of the gradient is lost.  In equilibrium the
latitudinal alpha-richness relationship that is observed is the neutral
speciation-immigration-drift gradient.  Competition driven, latitude
dependent erosion of diversity is a niche prediction and is absent under
strict neutrality.  That is the statement that the latitudinal alpha
diversity slope is maintained by neutral processes and is essentially
unchanged by the invasion, and in the limit of a perfectly good
disperser the system is driven towards the neutrally homogenised,
dispersal limited expectation, i.e. the apparent niche steepness of the
gradient is eroded and the slope flattens to the neutral baseline. ∎
public_text.13:
The alpha diversity–latitude slope is going to flatten out, i.e. the positive equator-ward gradient will become shallower over time.

Under Hubbell the local alpha richness is set by neutral drift in the context of a regional metacommunity, with immigration rescuing rare species and local community size setting the strength of drift. The latitudinal pattern you are seeing now is basically a neutral consequence of a larger regional species pool and higher effective immigration rates toward the equator, against which drift is comparatively weak.

Once the European invader is truly everywhere it becomes a high-frequency, high-dispersal member of the metacommunity that is present in all 12 sites. Because species are ecologically equivalent under neutrality, its impact is not an asymmetric competitive advantage but a change in the abundance distribution and in the effective size of the local pools that it occupies. Demographic stochasticity is strongest where local communities are smallest and where immigration is lowest, which is exactly the high-latitude end of your transect.

The invader will therefore rise to relative dominance faster in the small, low-immigration northern communities in Ottawa, State College and Charlotte than in the large, high-immigration tropical communities in Tena, Cali and Barro Colorado. Via neutral drift it will take up a larger fraction of the local abundance space and stochastically exclude rare natives in those northern sites, while the same absolute number of invader individuals is a much smaller proportional perturbation in the species-rich equatorial sites.

In the long run the metacommunity is homogenised by this ubiquitous, well-dispersed neutral taxon and local alpha richness becomes more similar across the transect. The equator remains richer in absolute terms, but the difference per degree latitude declines, so the fitted slope of alpha diversity against latitude flattens toward zero relative to the pre-invasion baseline.
public_text.12:
Under Hubbell the ecological identity of a species is irrelevant. Per
capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are by construction
identical for all lineages so that the per capita competitive ability
that is invoked in a niche explanation is set to zero. Alpha richness
at a local site of size J is then set by neutral demographic stochasticity,
immigration m from the regional metacommunity and the fundamental
biodiversity number

θ = 2Jm ν

with ν the per-lineage speciation rate. The expected local richness
is

E[Sα] ≈ θ[ ψ(J+θ) – ψ(θ) ]

and the familiar latitudinal increase of Sα towards the equator is the
neutrally generated consequence of a larger regional species pool and
in general higher m and/or larger J towards the tropics. It is a
property of the neutral birth–death–immigration–speciation process,
not of a latitudinally varying competitive superiority.

A lineage that is introduced from Europe and subsequently succeeds in
reaching every local community in the Americas is therefore in the
neutral model just another ecologically equivalent neutral lineage.
It can increase the regional pool by one, θ→θ+Δθ, and it is then
incorporated into each of the 12 local assemblages by the same neutral
drift/immigration dynamics that govern the natives. In expectation the
invasive is added to local alpha richness in a way that is independent
of latitude so that

Sα,post (lat)  ≈ Sα,pre (lat) + ΔS0

i.e. the species–latitude relationship is shifted upward in parallel.
In absolute numbers the difference Sα,tropics – Sα,temperate and hence
the slope dSα/d latitude is conserved. There is no neutrally predicted
competitive, latitudinally biased loss of natives: the potential to
“out-compete” that is postulated in niche terms is null under exact
neutrality.

If the strict zero-sum multinomial formulation is kept the total
number of individuals J is held constant so the invasive is accommodated
by neutral displacement of individuals rather than by a net increase in
Sα. The expectation is then an essentially unchanged latitudinal
gradient of alpha richness, the familiar neutral latitudinal diversity
gradient persisting with the invasive now simply part of the neutral
species abundance distribution. In proportional terms the additive
cosmopolitan species contributes most to the depauperate high-latitude
sites, which is the usual way of describing a neutral homogenising
effect: the gradient is conserved in absolute units and looks
marginally less steep in relative units, but there is no neutrally
predicted erosion or reversal of the equatorward increase in insect
alpha diversity. That is just the statement that under strict neutrality
competitive exclusion by the invasive does not exist.
public_text.11:
Under the UNTB all individuals are demographically equivalent and competitive
superiority in the niche sense is by definition removed.  Local alpha
richness at equilibrium is

Sα ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ]    θ =2Jm ν

a function only of local community size J, metacommunity size Jm and
the per capita speciation rate ν, and of the immigration rate m which
sets the coupling of the local community to the metacommunity.  The
latitudinal change in Sα that is seen now is therefore in a neutral
world a change in the neutral parameters J, m and ν with latitude, not
a change in the outcome of interspecific competition at the local scale.

In the neutral world the European invader is just another neutrally
equivalent species that is now part of the American metacommunity.  It
cannot “out-compete’’ natives in the niche sense, it can only increase
in local frequency by drift and by the flux of propagules that the now
pan-American species supplies to every local community.  The net effect
of a truly pan-American, good disperser is an increase in homogenising
immigration and therefore an increase in the similarity of local
communities to the regional pool and to each other, i.e. a loss of beta
diversity.  In the zero sum multinomial limit the long term Sα at each
site is set by J and m and by the metacommunity θ.  Adding one
neutrally equivalent, well dispersed species to the metacommunity does
not create a latitudinally biased competitive loss of natives.  In
particular it does not produce the niche expectation of a stronger
diversity loss in the species rich tropics than in the species poor
temperate sites.

In practice that means that the competitive exclusion story that
motivated the re-visit has no neutral counterpart.  The alpha – latitude
relationship is maintained by the neutral geography of speciation and
dispersal and is not amplified by the invasion.  With the now essentially
pan-continental source of propagules the neutral expectation is a
progressive homogenisation of the local communities and an erosion of
the observed alpha slope toward a flat, dispersal dominated Sα ~ const
across the transect.  In the strict equilibrium limit the slope is
conserved by the underlying neutral parameters J,m,ν and there is no
systematic, competition driven steepening or tropical-biased decline of
alpha diversity in the way a niche competitive exclusion picture would
predict.  That is the neutral null to which any observed competitive
decline would have to be compared.
public_text.14:
The latitudinal slope of alpha diversity will flatten over time and its magnitude will decline toward zero.

Under Hubbell’s unified neutral theory local alpha diversity is set by the balance of ecological drift, speciation and immigration into a local community from the regional metacommunity. The 12 sites span a classic latitudinal gradient in regional species pools and in effective immigration, so alpha diversity rises toward the equator simply because the equatorial metacommunity is larger and immigration limitation is weaker at low latitudes.

The European invader is now a high-dispersal member of the metacommunity that is present at every site from Ottawa to Tena. Because neutral theory treats species as ecologically equivalent, its fate is governed by drift and the immigration–extinction balance rather than by a competitive advantage. Once it is established it contributes a persistent source of propagules to the entire network. Immigration limitation is strongest at high-latitude sites where regional richness and propagule rain are naturally low. A widespread, highly mobile immigrant therefore raises local alpha diversity proportionally more in the north than in the already species saturated equatorial sites.

In effect the invader raises the effective regional theta and supplies a homogenising dispersal flux along the latitudinal axis. Beta diversity declines and the alpha values converge across the transect as the northern communities are ‘filled in’ faster than the southern ones. Re-measurement in the future should therefore show a shallower, less steep increase of insect alpha diversity toward the equator, with the slope progressively flattening as the gradient is eroded by neutral dispersal homogenisation.
public_text.17:
The latitudinal increase in alpha diversity is going to erode and the slope will flatten, essentially be attenuated toward zero.

Under Hubbell’s unified neutral theory local alpha richness at a site is a stochastic sample of the metacommunity set by community size, per capita speciation ν and per capita immigration m, not by species-specific competitive superiority. Once the European invader is present in the whole Americas it becomes a permanent, highly dispersive member of the metacommunity and is incorporated into the regional species abundance distribution on neutral terms. 

In practice that means effective immigration is raised and the regional pool is increasingly homogenised across the 12 localities. Sites that were previously limited by low immigration from a species-rich tropical source, i.e. the high-latitude sites, experience a relatively larger neutral boost in the number of individuals and species they can maintain from the now pan-American pool, while the already species saturated equatorial sites gain little and lose local species to drift as the invader joins the zero-sum lottery. 

That is the classic neutral expectation of biotic homogenisation: local communities converge toward the same neutral expectation set by the common metacommunity size and dispersal regime. The tropical excess generated by a higher tropical ν is progressively diluted by pan-continental dispersal and neutral drift, so the alpha diversity vs. latitude relationship loses its steepness. In the long term the observed north-south gradient in alpha diversity is flattened, with the slope decreasing in magnitude and approaching a much more even, low-gradient pattern across Tena to Ottawa.
public_text.16:
Under Hubbell’s neutral model local alpha diversity is essentially a random sample of the regional metacommunity, with the latitudinal increase in alpha richness reflecting a larger regional species pool / higher metacommunity theta towards the equator rather than any deterministic niche advantage. An introduced, highly dispersive species that establishes everywhere is just another ecologically equivalent draw from that metacommunity. 

Because it is able to drift to high relative abundance across the whole transect, it will displace native species proportionally to its abundance. The absolute number of native species displaced is therefore much larger where the regional pool and the expected local richness are largest. Tropical sites such as Tena, Cali and Barro Colorado Island start with a much larger alpha richness than Ottawa or State College, so the same neutral drift-induced increase in the frequency of the invader removes more species in absolute terms near the equator than at temperate sites. The temperate trough is eroded only modestly in absolute terms while the tropical peak is eroded strongly.

That asymmetric absolute loss attenuates the equator-to-pole increase in local richness, i.e. the latitudinal alpha diversity gradient is flattened. In the long neutral equilibrium the slope of alpha diversity vs latitude becomes less positive, with the tropical-temperate contrast reduced relative to the pre-invasion baseline, even though the rank order of sites is preserved.
public_text.21:
Under Hubbell’s neutral framework the latitudinal gradient in local alpha diversity is essentially an immigration-drift equilibrium set by metacommunity size and dispersal. The invader is now a cosmopolitan member of the New World metacommunity and, by neutrality, it is ecologically equivalent to the natives it replaces. That means its incorporation into local communities is governed by drift and immigration, not by superior competitive ability.

Immigration limitation is strongest at the high-latitude, low-diversity ends of the transect where local communities are smaller and drift is more effective at losing rare species. Adding a highly dispersive, now everywhere-present species to the regional pool therefore raises the expected local richness and, more importantly, the expected local abundance of a given metacommunity frequency, disproportionately in those immigration-limited sites. In the equatorial sites the local assemblage is already saturated with respect to the neutral immigration-drift balance and the species pool is large, so the proportional gain in alpha diversity from the new widespread neutral species is diluted.

The net effect is an increase in alpha diversity that is larger at high latitudes than at low latitudes, i.e., an upward shift that is steeper towards the pole. The latitudinal alpha diversity increase with decreasing latitude therefore becomes shallower, the slope of alpha diversity vs latitude flattens toward zero and the equator-to-pole contrast is reduced over time.
public_text.15:
Under Hubbell the latitudinal pattern of alpha diversity is not a niche 
pattern at all.  In the zero sum multinomial limit

* E[Slocal|J,theta] ~ f(theta ,J) ,      theta = 2Jm nu ,

where theta is the fundamental biodiversity number of the metacommunity
that feeds the local community, J is local community size and nu is the
per capita speciation rate.  The classic latitudinal increase in alpha
is the neutral emergent consequence of a latitudinal increase in the
regional theta, i.e. a larger regional species pool and, in the usual
formulation, a larger per capita speciation rate in the tropics, together
with dispersal limitation and zero sum demographic drift.  Species
identity and species specific competitive superiority are not parameters
of the model.

In neutral terms the European invader is just one more ecologically
equivalent draw from the regional pool.  It cannot be allowed a
persistent competitive advantage and its long term fate is that of any
other species, namely stochastic increase / decrease by demographic drift,
immigration and speciation/extinction.  Once the invader is present in
the continent-wide metacommunity it is present, at neutral expectation,
in every local community that is connected to the metacommunity and it
contributes the same, ecologically equivalent, increment to the zero sum
species abundance distribution everywhere. The competitive story that
is invoked in niche theory is therefore neutrally irrelevant in the
long run.

In the long run the system relaxes to the neutral equilibrium set by
regional theta, Jm and m and the latitudinal increase in alpha diversity
is maintained by the latitudinal increase in regional theta / speciation
and by drift/dispersal, not by the identity or competitive ability of any
single species.  Any transient loss of natives that is seen immediately
after the invasion is proportional to local richness and is swamped by
neutral drift/immigration so that the neutral expectation for the
alpha vs latitude relationship is recovered.  In the verbal shorthand
which is normally used this is described as neutral homogenisation:
the widespread common species increases mixing among sites, beta
diversity is reduced and the alpha diversity gradient is damped and in
the strict dispersal unlimited neutral limit is homogenised toward the
regional mean.  The persistent, competition driven steepening or
flattening of the alpha gradient that niche theory would predict does not
exist under neutrality; the gradient is a neutral emergent property and
in the ultimate neutral equilibrium it is essentially unchanged and is
set by speciation, drift and dispersal, not by the invasive’s ability to
out-compete natives.  That is the usual statement that the competitive
impact is transient and ultimately neutralised.
public_text.19:
Under the Unified Neutral Theory of Biodiversity and Biogeography all co-occurring species are ecologically equivalent and local community composition is the outcome of stochastic birth-death-immigration-speciation drift in a metacommunity. 

The classic latitudinal increase in local alpha diversity that you are seeing with
Tena > … > Ottawa is the neutral expectation for a set of communities sampled from
a metacommunity whose size, speciation rate and net immigration increase towards
the low latitudes. The putative ‘ability to out-compete many natives’ of the
European insect is therefore irrelevant for long-term community structure under
UNT. Competition in the sense of deterministic competitive exclusion does not
exist, it is replaced by neutral drift and regional dispersal.

At demographic equilibrium the invader becomes just one more neutrally sampled
species in the American insect metacommunity of the trophic level in question. In
the limit it is present in every local community and is sampled locally in
proportion to its metacommunity relative abundance. The net long-term effect
is therefore essentially a neutral addition of a widespread species to the
regional pool,

Smeta → Smeta +1

and a neutrally sampled addition to every local community,

Sα,i(t→∞) ≈ Sα,i0 + ΔSneut,i,

with ΔSneut,i ≃ 1 for all i. In absolute terms the local richness is
raised by essentially the same amount everywhere, so the latitudinal
α-diversity profile is translated up but is not systematically reshaped by
competition. The equatorial > tropical > temperate increase in alpha diversity,
i.e. the positive equatorial slope, is maintained by neutral drift, immigration
and the underlying gradient in metacommunity size/speciation. In proportional
terms the increment is a little larger at high-latitude, species-poor sites
because of the saturating neutral species–area/immigration relationship, so in
practice the gradient is essentially conserved and at most very slightly
flattened by the added cosmopolitan neutral element. There is no persistent
competition-driven loss of native alpha diversity and no long-term change in
the neutrally generated latitudinal slope produced by the invasion.
public_text.20:
Under strict neutrality there is no niche based competitive superiority and
hence no niche based competitive displacement.  In the unified neutral
theory all species in the metacommunity are ecologically equivalent and
local relative abundances are generated by stochastic ecological drift,
speciation at rate ν and dispersal–immigration at rate m.  The expected
local species richness in the zero-sum multinomial limit is a function of
the local community size J, the metacommunity parameter θ = 2νJ_M and the
immigration parameter m and in the limit m→0 it is set by the regional
speciation–immigration balance.  The classic equatorward increase in
alpha richness is then the neutral expectation of a higher long term
regional species pool θ in the tropics, i.e. effectively a higher net
speciation rate in the low latitude metacommunity, not the outcome of
local competitive exclusion.

In particular a species that is present in the metacommunity is just
another neutrally equivalent species.  The introduction of one
cosmopolitan neutral species adds essentially the same expected
increment to the local species pool at every locality in which it can
immigrate.  On average it is a uniform +1 to local richness when it is
present, or, in a zero sum formulation, a neutrally fluctuating
replacement, so that the between site pattern in Sα is not altered in a
latitudinally structured way. There is no neutral mechanism by which the
invasive can systematically out compete and remove more natives at low
latitude than at high latitude, or vice versa.  The latitudinal alpha
gradient therefore persists under neutrality.

In practice that means the biologically meaningful competition driven
change that the researchers are interested in is null under Hubbell.
Formally the expected alpha richness is increased essentially uniformly
by the cosmopolitan invader so that Sα,i(t→∞)=Sα,i(0)+Δ with Δ≈1
everywhere, i.e. the intercept of the Sα–latitude relationship is
raised a trivial amount and the slope dSα/d latitude remains positive
and essentially unchanged.  If the uniform addition is removed the
often quoted neutral statement is that a truly metacommunity-wide
disperser homogenises local composition and increases immigration–
mediated rescue at the species-poor high latitude end so that the
observed alpha gradient is slightly attenuated/flattened with time,
tending towards greater among-site homogenisation.  The flattening is a
dispersal homogenisation effect, not a competition driven loss of
natives, and in the strict neutral limit the equilibrium latitudinal
alpha gradient set by the latitudinal variation in θ and m is retained.
public_text.18:
Under a neutral metacommunity the fitness differences that are invoked in
the niche picture are by definition absent.

In the Hubbell zero-sum multinomial the local community at a site is just
a sample without replacement of a common regional pool.  Local  alpha
richness is

Sα ≈ f(θ , J , m )

where θ = 2Jmν is the fundamental biodiversity number of the
metacommunity, J the local community size and m the per capita
immigration probability.  Speciation ν, community size J and the
immigration / dispersal regime set the regional γ diversity and the
expected Sα at a site.  Ecological equivalence means that a species that
is introduced from Europe has no intrinsic competitive superiority to
native species in the same trophic level. Its fate in a local community
is that of any other species: increase or decrease in abundance
and the possibility of local extinction is set by demographic stochasticity
and immigration, not by deterministic competitive exclusion.

Hence the niche expectation that a superior invader will selectively
remove more native species in the species rich tropics and therefore
flatten the latitudinal alpha gradient is a niche prediction.  In the
strict neutral limit the invader is just one more ecologically equivalent
species drawn from the metacommunity.  On average it replaces a random
native species in the zero-sum lottery, so that to first order there is
no latitudinally biased loss of Sα.  In particular the classical
latitudinal alpha gradient, Sα↑ toward the equator, is the neutral
drift / immigration / speciation gradient

Sα,lat ≈ θlat ln[1+J/θlat]

and it is maintained by the latitudinal increase in ν and/or J and by
the metacommunity sampling effect, not by local competitive
displacement.  Ecologically, over ecological time scales the alpha
diversity–latitude relationship therefore stays essentially as it is
observed now, i.e. a positive slope Sα vs latitude with no systematic
neutrally-driven flattening produced by competitive exclusion.

In the limit of very high effective dispersal the widespread invader
makes the regional pool more homogeneous, β-diversity falls and the
local communities become more similar to the metacommunity mean.
That is the usual neutral homogenisation effect: any increase in
effective m raises Sα most in historically species poor, high-latitude
sites where Sα is far from the regional saturation curve and raises it
least in the species saturated tropics.  The net neutral effect is
therefore a weak tendency for the inter-site variance in Sα to shrink
and for the observed alpha-vs-latitude slope to weaken / flatten toward
the common metacommunity expectation, and in the idealised infinite
mixing limit the slope would tend to zero.  The important neutral
point is that the flattening, if it occurs, is a dispersal/drift
homogenisation effect, not a competitive displacement of tropical
natives by a superior invader.  In the conventional strict zero-sum
neutral formulation the slope is effectively conserved. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The UNTB framing is decisive: per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical for all species in the trophic level, so per-capita competitive superiority is null by construction. Local alpha richness is a neutral sampling outcome 
$S_{\alpha}\approx f\!\left[J,m,\theta\right]$, $\theta=2J_{m}\nu$, set by local community size $J$, immigration $m$ and the fundamental biodiversity number $\theta$ of the metacommunity that feeds the site. The observed equator-to-pole increase in $S_{\alpha}$ is therefore under neutrality a speciation/drift/dispersal gradient, essentially a latitudinally varying $\nu$ and metacommunity size, not a niche filtering gradient.

The European insect, once it reaches every site from Tena to Ottawa, is in the neutral limit just one more ecologically equivalent neutral lineage now part of the American metacommunity. It cannot systematically drive natives out by niche displacement. In expectation it is incorporated by the same zero-sum multinomial/ drift-immigration dynamics as any other species, with an occupancy that tends to one because of assumed rapid pan-continental dispersal.

That gives the neutral null to the niche competitive-exclusion story. To first order the whole $S_{\alpha}$ vs latitude curve is translated up in parallel by the essentially constant occupancy of a cosmopolitan neutral taxon,
$S_{\alpha}^{post}(lat)\approx S_{\alpha}^{pre}(lat)+ \Delta S_{0}$,
so the absolute difference $S_{\alpha,tropics}-S_{\alpha,temperate}$ and the absolute slope $dS_{\alpha}/d{\rm lat}$ set by the latitudinal $\nu/m/J$ gradient is conserved. No neutrally predicted, latitude-biased loss of native alpha richness occurs.

The debate in round 0 is about how that constant addition is expressed. A strict zero-sum formulation with a saturating neutral species-area/immigration relationship gives a diminishing marginal return $\partial S/\partial\theta>0$, $\partial^{2}S/\partial\theta^{2}<0$. Hence a ubiquitous species raises $S_{\alpha}$ proportionally more where $S_{\alpha}$ is initially low, i.e. at high-latitude immigration-limited sites, and relatively less at species-saturated equatorial sites. Colleagues 13,14,2,7,21 etc describe this as neutral homogenisation / biotic homogenisation: beta diversity falls, the alpha gradient is damped and in relative/proportional terms the slope $d\ln S_{\alpha}/d{\rm lat}$ looks flatter, tending toward the metacommunity mean under strong mixing.

Colleagues 1,10,12,19,20,18,8 argue the core neutral statement is slope conservation in absolute units; any flattening is a second-order dispersal-homogenisation effect, not a competition-driven tropical loss, and the qualitative equatorward increase persists as the neutral speciation-drift gradient.

Unresolved nuance: whether to report the effect as strictly conserved absolute slope with a parallel upward shift, versus the practically often-quoted slight neutral homogenisation/flattening in proportional terms due to saturating richness and increased effective $m$ from a pan-American source. The competition-driven, latitude-dependent erosion of tropical diversity predicted by niche theory is neutrally absent, which is the main point the question targets.

I retain the latitudinal $\nu$, $m$, $J$ drivers, ecological equivalence, zero-sum neutral sampling, and the distinction between absolute slope conservation and relative homogenisation.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The 12 sites span a classic pole-to-equator alpha gradient. Under Hubbell UNTB all species in the trophic level are ecologically equivalent; per-capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical, so species-specific competitive superiority is null. Local alpha at equilibrium is set by neutral sampling of the metacommunity: Sα ≈ f(J, m, θ) with θ = 2Jm ν, the fundamental biodiversity number. The observed latitudinal increase in Sα is therefore neutrally interpreted as a latitudinal gradient in regional θ / speciation ν and effective immigration m, not as niche filtering/competition.

The European invader is, in the neutral limit, just one more ecologically equivalent lineage now part of the American metacommunity. With pan-American spread it becomes a ubiquitous, high m species. In zero-sum neutral dynamics it can only replace individuals randomly; there is no systematic latitudinally biased competitive loss of natives.

That gives the core neutral null: a competition-driven tropical loss of diversity does not exist. In absolute terms the invasion adds essentially a latitude-independent occupancy ≈ \hat{x}_{inv} to each local community, Sα(lat) → Sα(lat)+ΔS0, so the absolute difference Sα,tropics – Sα,temperate and dSα/dlat set by the underlying ν(lat), m(lat), J gradient is conserved and the curve is shifted up in parallel. The latitudinal alpha gradient persists as the speciation-drift-immigration gradient.

A secondary neutral effect is homogenising dispersal. Adding a cosmopolitan neutral taxon raises effective immigration/connectivity; beta diversity declines and local communities converge toward the metacommunity mean. Because Sα(θ,J) is saturating, ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0, the proportional gain from a ubiquitous species is larger where Sα is initially low i.e. high-latitude, species-poor sites, and smaller at saturated equatorial sites. In proportional terms d ln Sα / d lat is weakly reduced and the among-site variance in Sα tends to shrink. Several colleagues frame this as a flattening/homogenisation of the gradient toward zero in the well-mixed m→1 limit.

$S_{\alpha}^{post}(lat)\approx S_{\alpha}^{pre}(lat)+ \Delta S_{0}$,
so the absolute difference $S_{\alpha,tropics}-S_{\alpha,temperate}$ and the absolute slope $dS_{\alpha}/d{\rm lat}$ set by the latitudinal $\nu/m/J$ gradient is conserved. No neutrally predicted, latitude-biased loss of native alpha richness occurs.

The debate in round 0 is about how that constant addition is expressed. A strict zero-sum formulation with a saturating neutral species-area/immigration relationship gives a diminishing marginal return $\partial S/\partial\theta>0$, $\partial^{2}S/\partial\theta^{2}<0$. Hence a ubiquitous species raises $S_{\alpha}$ proportionally more where $S_{\alpha}$ is initially low, i.e. at high-latitude immigration-limited sites, and relatively less at species-saturated equatorial sites. Colleagues 13,14,2,7,21 etc describe this as neutral homogenisation / biotic homogenisation: beta diversity falls, the alpha gradient is damped and in relative/proportional terms the slope $d\ln S_{\alpha}/d{\rm lat}$ looks flatter, tending toward the metacommunity mean under strong mixing.

Colleagues 1,10,12,19,20,18,8 argue the core neutral statement is slope conservation in absolute units; any flattening is a second-order dispersal-homogenisation effect, not a competition-driven tropical loss, and the qualitative equatorward increase persists as the neutral speciation-drift gradient.

Unresolved nuance: whether to report the effect as strictly conserved absolute slope with a parallel upward shift, versus the practically often-quoted slight neutral homogenisation/flattening in proportional terms due to saturating richness and increased effective $m$ from a pan-American source. The competition-driven, latitude-dependent erosion of tropical diversity predicted by niche theory is neutrally absent, which is the main point the question targets.

I retain the latitudinal $\nu$, $m$, $J$ drivers, ecological equivalence, zero-sum neutral sampling, and the distinction between absolute slope conservation and relative homogenisation.
reflection_text.11:
The 12 sites span a classic pole-to-equator alpha gradient. Under Hubbell UNTB all species in the trophic level are ecologically equivalent; per-capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical, so species-specific competitive superiority is null. Local alpha at equilibrium is set by neutral sampling of the metacommunity: Sα ≈ f(J, m, θ) with θ = 2Jm ν, the fundamental biodiversity number. The observed latitudinal increase in Sα is therefore neutrally interpreted as a latitudinal gradient in regional θ / speciation ν and effective immigration m, not as niche filtering/competition.

The European invader is, in the neutral limit, just one more ecologically equivalent lineage now part of the American metacommunity. With pan-American spread it becomes a ubiquitous, high m species. In zero-sum neutral dynamics it can only replace individuals randomly; there is no systematic latitudinally biased competitive loss of natives.

That gives the core neutral null: a competition-driven tropical loss of diversity does not exist. In absolute terms the invasion adds essentially a latitude-independent occupancy ≈ \hat{x}_{inv} to each local community, Sα(lat) → Sα(lat)+ΔS0, so the absolute difference Sα,tropics – Sα,temperate and dSα/dlat set by the underlying ν(lat), m(lat), J gradient is conserved and the curve is shifted up in parallel. The latitudinal alpha gradient persists as the speciation-drift-immigration gradient.

A secondary neutral effect is homogenising dispersal. Adding a cosmopolitan neutral taxon raises effective immigration/connectivity; beta diversity declines and local communities converge toward the metacommunity mean. Because Sα(θ,J) is saturating, ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0, the proportional gain from a ubiquitous species is larger where Sα is initially low i.e. high-latitude, species-poor sites, and smaller at saturated equatorial sites. In proportional terms d ln Sα / d lat is weakly reduced and the among-site variance in Sα tends to shrink. Several colleagues frame this as a flattening/homogenisation of the gradient toward zero in the well-mixed m→1 limit.

Disagreement in the round: 
- Maintain/conserve slope camp: Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,19,20,8 argue the slope is essentially unchanged in absolute units, with at most a trivial parallel upward shift; flattening if any is a dispersal homogenisation artefact, not competitive displacement.
- Flatten/homogenise camp: Colleagues 13,14,2,16,17,21,3,4,5,7,9 argue the ubiquitous invader raises the northern floor faster than the tropical ceiling, leading to neutral biotic homogenisation and a shallower equatorward slope over time.

Unresolved tension is whether the strict zero-sum neutral prediction is exact slope conservation with a uniform ΔS, or a weak flattening due to saturating S(θ) and increased effective m.
