reflection_text.12:
The 12 sites span a classic equator-to-pole alpha gradient. Under Hubbell UNTB all species in the trophic level are ecologically equivalent; per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical. Local alpha is Sα ≈ f[J,m,θ] with θ = 2Jmν, i.e. a function of local community size, immigration rate and the fundamental biodiversity number set by regional speciation and metacommunity size. The observed latitudinal increase in Sα is therefore a neutral speciation/dispersal/drift gradient, not a local competitive advantage gradient.

The invasive European insect is, in the neutral limit, just another neutral lineage. It has no intrinsic per capita competitive advantage and cannot systematically drive residents out by niche displacement. Long term its fate is drift + immigration from a now pan-American metacommunity. In strict zero-sum with constant J the invader is incorporated by neutral replacement; in the additive approximation it adds essentially the same expected occupancy ΔS≈1 to every site that it can reach.

That gives the neutral null: no latitude-biased competitive loss of natives. In absolute terms Sα(lat) → Sα0(lat)+ const, so dSα/dlat is conserved and the equatorward increase is maintained. The species-latitude relationship is shifted up in parallel. Competition-driven tropical loss is absent.

A second line in the discussion argues for neutral homogenisation/flattening. A ubiquitous high-m species raises effective connectivity and homogenises the metacommunity. Immigration limitation is strongest at high-latitude, species-poor sites. Adding a cosmopolitan neutral taxon therefore raises α proportionally more in the north than in the already saturated tropics, reduces β-diversity, and in proportional terms d ln Sα/dlat weakens. The flattening described here is a dispersal/drift homogenisation effect, not a niche competitive exclusion effect, and in the idealised m→1 limit the gradient would be erased.

Disagreement in the colleagues is exactly absolute vs proportional slope and how far the zero-sum constraint is applied. Strict equivalence defenders 1,10,12,19,20 say slope is essentially conserved, at most a very weak proportional homogenisation. Homogenisation defenders 13,14,16,17,2,21,4,5,7,9 say the gradient is eroded and flattens toward zero because the widespread invader pushes northern sites up toward the regional mean while tropical sites are diluted by drift/replacement.

Unresolved for me: whether the neutral saturation curve makes the additive +1 effectively latitude-independent in absolute units or produces the classic diminishing returns flattening in proportional units, and how the zero-sum formulation changes the sign of the long-term change. The key neutral point I need to keep is that any systematic latitude-dependent loss of native α by “out-competing” is a niche prediction and is null under exact neutrality.
reflection_text.8:
The core neutral premise is being reiterated by all colleagues: under Hubbell UNTB species are ecologically equivalent, per capita birth/death/immigration/speciation are identical and “out-compete” has no neutral meaning. Local alpha Sα is a sampling outcome of a regional metacommunity set by J, m and the fundamental biodiversity number θ = 2Jm ν, with the classic equatorward increase in Sα being a neutral speciation/drift/immigration gradient, not niche filtering.

What is in dispute is the long-term effect of a pan-American, highly dispersive invader on the latitudinal Sα–latitude slope.

Maintain/parallel-shift camp: 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,8,6. Invader is just another neutrally equivalent draw. It is incorporated into the metacommunity by drift/immigration and, in expectation, adds essentially the same occupancy to every site, Sα,post(lat) ≈ Sα,pre(lat)+ΔS0, with ΔS0≈1 and latitude independent. In absolute units dSα/dlat and the tropical-temperate absolute difference are therefore conserved. In zero-sum the species replaces individuals at random; no latitudinally biased loss of natives occurs. Any proportional flattening is only the saturating Sα ~ θ ln[1+J/θ] effect: a constant addition raises species-poor northern sites more in relative terms than species-rich equatorial sites.

Flatten/homogenise camp: 13,14,2,21,4,5,7,9,16,17,3. A ubiquitous high-m species raises effective connectivity and homogenises the metacommunity, i.e. reduces β-diversity. Immigration limitation is strongest at high latitudes; the widespread invader therefore raises local richness proportionally more in the north than in the already saturated tropics, and via neutral drift removes more rare natives in absolute numbers where richness is initially largest. The net neutral expectation is convergence of local alpha toward a common metacommunity mean, progressive erosion of the north-south contrast and a shallower, eventually near-flat Sα vs latitude relationship. The flattening is described as dispersal/drift homogenisation, not competition-driven tropical loss.

Common ground: no neutral mechanism produces the niche prediction of a competition-driven, latitude-dependent erosion of tropical alpha. The putative competitive superiority is null under exact neutrality. The gradient that remains is the neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient set by a latitudinally varying ν and regional θ.

Unresolved for me: how to weigh strict zero-sum sampling, which predicts an essentially latitude-independent additive/parallel shift and conservation of absolute slope, against the homogenising-immigration interpretation that a truly pan-continental disperser raises m effectively and drives alpha toward the regional mean, giving a flattening of the observed slope. The verbal shorthand in the literature is often a weak neutral homogenisation/flattening of the proportional gradient while the absolute neutral gradient set by speciation persists. That tension between “slope conserved in absolute units” vs “slope declines toward zero with dispersal homogenisation” is the key point to track in later rounds.
reflection_text.3:
The question is about the long-term latitudinal alpha-diversity slope under Hubbell UNTB for a now pan-American invasive in the same trophic level that is claimed to be able to out-compete natives in niche terms.

* In the strict neutral limit the European insect has no intrinsic competitive advantage. It is “just another” neutral lineage that becomes part of the American metacommunity pool
* With essentially pan-continental dispersal it becomes a ubiquitous, high-frequency immigrant. In expectation it is sampled locally in proportion to its metacommunity relative abundance
* In a zero-sum formulation the invader can only replace individuals stochastically. To first order Sα,post(lat) ≈ Sα,pre(lat)+ΔS0 with ΔS0 essentially latitude-independent, i.e. a parallel upward shift of the alpha-vs-latitude curve. The absolute difference Sα,tropics–Sα,temperate and dSα/dlat set by ν(lat), J and m is conserved

Disagreements in the round:
* Strict conservation view: colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,19,20,6,8 argue the latitudinal gradient is maintained by the underlying neutral geography of speciation/drift/dispersal. * Homogenisation/flattening view: colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,3,4,5,7,9,21 argue a ubiquitous well-dispersed neutral taxon raises effective immigration/connectivity, increases neutral homogenisation and reduces β diversity. Immigration limitation is strongest at high latitude, so the proportional gain in Sα is larger in the north and the invader causes larger absolute loss of rare natives where Sα is initially high. Long term the alpha values converge toward the regional mean, the fitted slope dSα/dlat declines in magnitude and in the idealised infinite-mixing limit tends to zero.

What I retain:
* Competition-driven tropical loss is a niche prediction and is neutrally absent.
* The neutral null is no systematic latitude-biased competitive erosion; the gradient is a drift/immigration/speciation emergent property.
* The mechanistic tension is between a strict parallel shift with slope conserved in absolute units versus a neutral dispersal homogenisation effect that weakens the gradient in proportional / variance terms. The classic textbook statement is that under strict neutrality the alpha-latitude relationship persists and the invasion is neutrally neutral, with at most a weak homogenising flattening that is a dispersal/drift effect, not competitive exclusion. Unresolved is how strongly to weight the homogenisation argument versus the formal zero-sum parallel shift.

Current leaning: under exact UNTB the competitive potential is irrelevant and the latitudinal alpha increase is maintained by ν(lat) and drift/immigration; the slope is essentially conserved in absolute terms, i.e. the curve is shifted up in parallel. reflection_text.15:
The initial problem is a neutral null for a niche competition story. Under Hubbell’s UNTB all individuals in the trophic level are ecologically equivalent; per-capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical. Local alpha richness is a sampling/drift outcome

Sα≈f(J,m,θ) with θ=2Jmν, θ being the fundamental biodiversity number set by regional speciation ν and metacommunity size. The observed equatorward increase in Sα from Ottawa → Tena is in the neutral picture a speciation/immigration/drift gradient, not a gradient in competitive ability.

Key points raised in round 0:
* The invader has no systematic per-capita competitive advantage under strict neutrality. Its fate is drift + immigration like any other species.
* In the zero-sum multinomial limit the invader can only replace individuals at random. With pan-American dispersal it becomes a ubiquitous, high-frequency member of the metacommunity.
* First-order effect is an essentially latitude-independent addition/occupancy: Sα,post(lat)≈Sα,pre(lat)+ΔS0 with ΔS0≈ the neutral occupancy of one cosmopolitan species. Absolute differences Sα,tropics–Sα,temperate and dSα/dlat are therefore conserved. The alpha-latitude curve is translated upward in parallel.
* In proportional terms the saturating neutral species-area/immigration relationship means a constant additive species raises relative richness more at species-poor high-latitude sites than at species-rich equatorial sites, so d ln Sα/dlat is weakly homogenised. This is dispersal homogenisation, not competition-driven tropical loss.
* Several colleagues argue for a strong flattening to zero, invoking that a ubiquitous disperser raises effective m and homogenises β-diversity, that drift loss of rare natives is larger where Sα is initially larger, and that low-latitude communities are near saturation while high-latitude communities are lifted toward the regional mean. This is the neutral homogenisation narrative.
* Others stress the strict zero-sum formulation: θ and ν(lat) maintain the latitudinal theta gradient, so the neutral speciation-drift gradient persists. The “out-compete” claim is null under exact neutrality; the competitive exclusion story is a niche prediction.

Unresolved tension: absolute slope conservation vs relative slope flattening/homogenisation. The text-book neutral statement is maintenance of the latitudinal alpha gradient set by ν,m,J, with at most a weak flattening in relative/proportional units due to a common cosmopolitan taxon and increased mixing. No neutrally predicted, latitude-biased competitive erosion of tropical alpha diversity.

My current synthesis leans to the strict neutral null: no systematic competition-driven change in the slope; the gradient is the neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient and is essentially retained, with only a trivial parallel upward shift and a mild, second-order homogenising effect in proportional terms. reflection_text.4:
The question is about the neutral null for a latitudinal alpha-diversity gradient under Hubbell UNTB with a now pan-American invasive.

Core neutral premises repeatedly invoked by colleagues:
* All species in the trophic level are ecologically equivalent; per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical. Competitive superiority in the niche sense is by construction absent.
* Local alpha richness at equilibrium is Sα ≈ f[J, m, θ] with θ = 2Jmν, the fundamental biodiversity number. The classic equatorward increase is a neutral speciation / drift / immigration effect – larger regional θ and/or larger m / J toward the tropics, not local competitive filtering.

Implications for the invader:
* The European insect is, in the neutral limit, just another neutrally equivalent member of the American metacommunity. It cannot systematically drive residents out. Its long-term fate is drift + immigration.
* With rapid range-wide dispersal it becomes a high-frequency, essentially ubiquitous source. In the zero-sum multinomial sampling picture it is incorporated into every local community with a latitude-independent expected occupancy.
* To first order Sα,post(lat) ≈ Sα,pre(lat) + ΔS0 with ΔS0 ≈ constant across sites. Hence in absolute numbers the latitudinal difference Sα,tropics – Sα,temperate and the absolute slope dSα/dlat are conserved; the whole alpha vs latitude curve is shifted up in parallel. The putative niche competition-driven, latitude-biased loss of natives is null under neutrality.

Where disagreement appears:
* Strict absolute conservation vs apparent homogenisation. Because Sα(θ) is concave/saturating, ∂S/∂θ >0, ∂²S/∂θ² <0, a constant additive cosmopolitan species raises proportional richness more at low-diversity, high-latitude sites than at high-diversity equatorial sites. Several colleagues frame this as neutral homogenisation / biotic homogenisation: beta diversity falls, the gradient is damped and in proportional terms d ln Sα/dlat is reduced.
* Some colleagues push the homogenisation to a limit: with a truly pan-continental, high-m disperser immigration limitation is relaxed at the north, the metacommunity is more mixed and the alpha gradient is eroded/flattened toward a common neutral expectation, with the slope tending toward zero in the idealised m→1 panmixing limit.
* Others stress that the underlying latitudinal variation in ν and regional θ is retained in the neutral model, so the neutrally generated alpha-latitude gradient persists and the invasion does not produce a competition-mediated steepening or tropical-biased decline; the flattening, if any, is a dispersal/drift homogenisation effect, not competitive exclusion.

Current synthesis:
I am leaning to the strict neutral statement: no systematic competitive displacement, so the competition-motivated erosion of the tropical peak is absent. The equilibrium alpha-latitude slope set by neutral speciation/drift/dispersal is maintained in absolute units, with at most a trivial parallel upward shift due to the new ubiquitous neutral species. The commonly quoted “flattening” is a proportional/ homogenisation description – the additive cosmopolitan species contributes a larger fractional increase at species-poor northern sites – and is not a niche competition effect. The unresolved tension is how much the diminishing returns / increased effective m changes the absolute slope vs only the proportional slope.

Remaining open points: precise zero-sum vs non-zero-sum formulation for the expected ΔSα; whether the invader also raises effective metacommunity θ by Δθ and whether that Δθ is latitude independent; and the exact timescale at which transient niche-like displacement is swamped by neutral drift.

reflection_text.20:
The question is about the long-term latitudinal slope of site-level alpha diversity under Hubbell UNTB after a European insect becomes pan-American.

Core neutral premises that are shared across almost all colleagues:
* UNTB: per capita birth, death, immigration, speciation are identical for all species; no niche competitive superiority. Species identity is irrelevant.
* Local alpha Sα ≈ f(J, m, θ) with θ = 2 Jm ν, the fundamental biodiversity number. Latitudinal increase in Sα now is a neutral speciation/dispersal/drift gradient, not local competition.
* The invader is therefore just another neutrally equivalent lineage in the American metacommunity. Its fate is drift + immigration, not deterministic out-competition.

Two camps on the slope outcome:

Maintained / essentially parallel shift camp – Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,6,8
* Adding a cosmopolitan neutral species gives Sα(lat) → Sα(lat)+ ΔS0 ≈ Sα(lat)+const, or in strict zero-sum a random replacement. To first order the alpha-latitude curve is translated up in parallel.
* Absolute difference Sα tropics – Sα temperate and dSα/dlat is conserved by the underlying latitudinal variation in ν,m,J. No neutrally predicted latitudinally biased loss of natives.
* If reported in proportional terms the ubiquitous species raises species-poor northern sites by a larger fraction, so d ln Sα/dlat is weakly homogenised, but absolute slope is maintained. The flattening is homogenisation/dispersal, not competitive exclusion.

Flatten/homogenise camp – Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,21,3,4,5,7,9
* A pan-American, high-dispersal invader raises effective connectivity and homogenises the metacommunity. Immigration limitation is strongest at high latitudes, so the invader raises alpha proportionally more in the north than in already saturated equatorial sites.
* Drift loss of rare natives is largest where local richness is largest, so the tropical excess is eroded in absolute terms while temperate sites are “filled in”. Beta diversity declines and alpha values converge.
* Net effect is a shallower, less steep increase towards the equator, slope magnitude declines toward zero in the well-mixed limit.

Points of tension / unresolved:
* Zero-sum vs non-zero sum formulation: strict zero-sum keeps J constant so invasion is replacement; non-zero allows a uniform +1 increment. Both give different verbal flattening statements.
* Whether θ is globally increased by +1 species or whether the invasion effectively increases m everywhere. Some treat it as a uniform additive species, others as an increase in homogenising immigration.
* The distinction between absolute slope conservation vs proportional flattening. Many colleagues acknowledge a weak neutral homogenisation in proportional terms even while claiming absolute conservation.

Current synthesis: Under strict neutrality there is no competition-driven tropical loss; the latitudinal alpha gradient set by speciation and drift is the neutral null. The invasion cannot produce niche-like competitive erosion. The neutral expectation is at best a parallel upward shift with conserved absolute dSα/dlat, and at most a mild dispersal-mediated homogenisation that attenuates the proportional slope. The stronger claim of slope → 0 is a homogenisation narrative that conflates neutral drift with niche competitive displacement. The core disagreement is whether that homogenisation is strong enough to flatten the absolute slope or merely weakens relative differences.

Unresolved for later rounds: How to treat J constancy, how m is altered by a ubiquitous disperser, and how to formalise the ‘flattening’ as a change in θ(lat) vs a change in sampling variance.
reflection_text.10:
The 12 sites span a latitudinal speciation/dispersal gradient. Under Hubbell UNTB local alpha richness is a neutral sampling outcome

Sα ≈ f[J,m,θ], θ = 2Jmν

set by local community size, immigration and the fundamental biodiversity number. The observed equatorward increase in Sα is therefore a neutral speciation/drift/immigration gradient, not a niche competitive gradient.

Ecological equivalence removes per capita competitive superiority. The European insect, once pan-American, is in the neutral limit just another ecologically equivalent member of the regional pool. Its fate is drift + immigration, not deterministic exclusion. The niche expectation of a latitude-biased loss of natives has no neutral counterpart.

Core consensus across colleagues:
* No systematic competition-driven erosion of tropical alpha. The invasion cannot generate a niche-style competitive displacement.
* In expectation the invader is incorporated into the metacommunity species abundance distribution and is sampled locally in proportion to its metacommunity frequency. In zero-sum terms it replaces individuals/stochastically replaces species rather than deterministically out-competing.

Disagreement is about the magnitude of the change in the Sα vs latitude slope:
* Strict absolute conservation view: Sα,post(lat) ≈ Sα,pre(lat)+ΔS0 with ΔS0 essentially latitude independent. The whole alpha-latitude curve is translated up in parallel, dSα/dlat is conserved in absolute units. Proportional increase is larger at species-poor high-latitude sites so d ln Sα/dlat is weakly homogenised/flattened, but the neutral speciation gradient persists.
* Homogenisation/flattening view: a ubiquitous high-dispersal neutral taxon raises effective connectivity and regional θ. Because the neutral Sα–θ relation is saturating, the additive ubiquitous species raises alpha more in proportional terms at the low-diversity, immigration-limited northern end than at the species-saturated tropical end. Drift loss is larger in absolute terms where standing richness is larger. That is described as neutral biotic homogenisation, beta diversity decline and a progressive shallowing of the alpha-latitude slope toward the regional mean, in the idealised m→1 limit → zero slope.

The most defensible neutral null is that competition is irrelevant: the latitudinal alpha gradient is maintained by the latitudinal variation in ν/m/J and the invasion does not produce a latitudinally biased competitive loss. The formal statement is a parallel upward shift with the absolute slope essentially conserved; the commonly quoted “flattening’’ is a dispersal-homogenisation / proportional effect, not a competition-driven tropical decline. reflection_text.6:
The discussion is now centered on what the neutral null does to a latitudinal alpha gradient when a highly dispersive European insect becomes pan-American.

Core neutral commitments that keep recurring:
* Under UNTB all individuals in the trophic guild are ecologically equivalent. Per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical. Species-specific competitive superiority is set to zero.
* Local alpha Sα is a neutral sampling outcome of a regional metacommunity: Sα ≈ f(J, m, θ) with θ = 2Jm ν the fundamental biodiversity number. The classic equator-to-pole increase in Sα is therefore a neutral speciation/dispersal/drift gradient, a latitudinal variation in θ / m / J, not a niche filtering effect.

Implications for the invader:
* In neutral terms the invader is just another ecologically equivalent lineage that is now part of the American metacommunity. It has no systematic ability to out-compete natives; its increase is governed by drift and immigration.
* In the long run it becomes a ubiquitous high-frequency element with essentially latitude-independent occupancy. To first order Sα(lat) → Sα(lat)+Δ with Δ ≈ occupancy of the cosmopolitan neutral species. In absolute numbers the tropical–temperate difference Sα(tropics)-Sα(temperate) is therefore conserved and the alpha–latitude relationship is translated up in parallel.
* In a zero-sum formulation the invader can only replace individuals at random. The competitive exclusion story that motivated the re-visit is neutrally irrelevant. There is no neutrally predicted, latitudinally biased loss of native alpha richness and no neutrally driven collapse/reversal of the gradient.

Points of disagreement/nuance that are still live:
* Proportional vs absolute slope. Because Sα(θ) is saturating, ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0, a uniform addition of a ubiquitous species raises species-poor high-latitude sites proportionally more than species-rich equatorial sites. Colleagues 1,10,12,19,20,6 emphasise this as a weak homogenisation in proportional terms, an essentially conserved absolute slope and a parallel upward shift; colleagues 13,14,16,17,21,2,4,5,7,9 push the homogenisation further and describe a progressive flattening/erosion of the gradient toward greater among-site similarity.
* Homogenisation of beta diversity. A pan-continental high-m species raises effective connectivity, reduces beta diversity and raises the floor of alpha at immigration-limited northern sites more than the ceiling at already saturated tropical sites. Whether that is phrased as “slope maintained“ or “slope flattened“ depends on whether slope is reported in absolute species per degree latitude or in relative/proportional terms.
* Zero-sum vs non-zero-sum. In strict zero-sum J is fixed, so the invader is accommodated by random displacement of natives; the neutrally expected latitudinal profile is retained. If the model is allowed a non-zero marginal increase, the gradient is shifted up but the sign of dSα/dlat remains positive.

Current leaning:
The competition-driven tropical loss of alpha diversity is null under exact neutrality. The latitudinal alpha gradient that is observed now is the neutral speciation/immigration/drift gradient and it persists. The invasion does not generate a niche-like competitive steepening or a competition-mediated flattening; at most it produces a weak neutral homogenisation that is a dispersal/drift effect, not competitive exclusion. The essential neutral null is maintenance of a positive equatorward alpha slope with any change being a latitude-independent upward shift and/or a modest proportional flattening due to saturating Sα(θ), not a loss of tropical diversity by out-competition.

Unresolved: how strongly the saturating Sα(θ) effect should be reported as a flattening of the fitted slope, and the exact treatment of J constant zero-sum vs an effective increase in θ from adding a cosmopolitan lineage.

reflection_text.19:
The core Hubbell UNTB setup is now clear to me: species in the trophic level are ecologically equivalent, per capita birth/death/immigration/speciation are identical, and local alpha richness is a neutral sampling outcome of local J, immigration m and the metacommunity fundamental biodiversity number θ =2Jmν. The observed equator-to-pole increase in Sα is therefore a neutral speciation/dispersal/drift gradient, ν(lat) and/or regional pool θ(lat) rising toward the equator, not a niche competition gradient.

The invasive European insect is, by construction, not a superior competitor under neutrality. Its long-term fate is that of any other neutral lineage: it can only rise/fall by drift and immigration flux, and once it is pan-American it becomes a ubiquitous, high-m member of the American metacommunity. That removes the niche expectation of latitudinally biased competitive loss of natives, especially in the species-rich tropics.

The disagreement in the round is about how the equilibrium Sα(lat) curve is translated.

* Parallel-shift / conserved-slope view: Colleagues 1,10,12,15,19,20 argue that in expectation the invader adds an essentially latitude-independent increment to local richness, Sα,post(lat)≈Sα,pre(lat)+c, or in zero-sum neutral replacement it is a random replacement. Absolute ΔSα tropics-north is therefore preserved, dSα/dlat is maintained, and the latitudinal gradient is the neutral speciation/drift gradient. Any proportional flattening is a secondary, non-competitive homogenisation effect.

* Homogenisation / flattening view: Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21,2,4,5,7,9 argue that a truly cosmopolitan disperser raises effective regional connectivity m and supplies a constant propagule rain. Immigration limitation is strongest at high latitude, low-diversity sites, so the proportional gain in alpha is larger northward and drift loss of rare natives is larger in absolute terms where Sα is initially large. That pushes local communities toward a common neutral expectation, reduces β-diversity and erodes the alpha-latitude slope toward zero, with tropical sites losing more absolute species in expectation because of zero-sum replacement.

* Intermediate statements note the saturating neutral species-area / immigration curve: ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0, so a uniform increase in regional θ or addition of a widespread neutral species raises Sα more in proportional terms at species-poor northern sites than at saturated tropical sites. That yields a weak flattening in relative terms while absolute slope is essentially conserved.

Unresolved for me: zero-sum vs non-zero-sum formulation and whether the introduction is best modelled as a constant +1 occupancy everywhere vs a small increase in metacommunity θ. If the model is kept strictly zero-sum with fixed J, the expected mean Sα at equilibrium is set by the latitudinal θ(lat) and m(lat) that are unchanged by the invasion, so the competition-driven steepening/flattening is null and the slope is conserved. The flattening arguments are really dispersal homogenisation / reduced β-diversity, not a neutral competitive exclusion mechanism.

Current leaning: Under strict neutrality the competitive out-compete story is null. The neutral null prediction is maintenance of the latitudinal alpha gradient set by speciation/drift/immigration, with at most a latitude-independent parallel upward shift of the curve and a weak homogenising tendency in proportional terms. A strong systematic erosion of the slope by competitive displacement is a niche prediction absent in Hubbell.

Because Sα(J,θ) is saturating, ΔSα from an increase in the regional pool/connectivity is diminishing in θ. The high-latitude sites — Ottawa, State College, Charlotte — are immigration limited and start far below the regional saturation curve. The same ubiquitous neutral propagule pressure therefore produces a proportionally larger increase in expected local richness at the north, whereas the equatorial sites — Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado — are already close to saturation for the given J and have a much larger standing pool of rare species that is vulnerable to neutral drift and replacement by the now high-frequency cosmopolitan.

In expectation the invader rises to relative dominance faster where drift is stronger and local communities are smaller, i.e. northwards, and it displaces rare natives stochastically. The net neutral effect is a loss of beta diversity and convergence of alpha across the transect: the floor is raised in the species poor north and the ceiling is eroded in relative terms in the species rich tropics. That is the textbook neutral homogenisation effect.

Formally the first-order absolute derivative can be written as conserved if you treat the addition as Sα(lat) → Sα(lat)+c, but that is the m≈0, additive bookkeeping limit. With fixed local J and zero-sum replacement the addition is not latitude independent in effect: the marginal gain dSα/dθ >0 but d²Sα/dθ²<0, so the proportional gain is larger where Sα is initially low. Empirically reported slopes are proportional changes per degree latitude, and the gradient is visibly damped.

So we should expect the positive equatorward alpha gradient to be maintained in rank order but to become progressively shallower, with the slope dSα/dlat declining in magnitude and tending toward greater among-site homogenisation as dispersal homogenisation proceeds. In the idealised well-mixed limit the gradient is erased. That is a neutral, drift-immigration homogenisation prediction, not a niche competitive exclusion story.

Under strict Hubbell neutrality the invasion is not a niche displacement event, it is the incorporation of one more ecologically equivalent draw into an already drift immigration limited metacommunity, and that incorporation is homogenising.

Local alpha in the zero sum formulation is Sα ≈ f(J, m, θ) with θ = 2Jmν. The equator to pole increase we see now is a neutral speciation immigration drift gradient: θ(lat) and effective m(lat) are larger toward the equator, so the neutral expectation Sα(λ) is larger there. The European insect does not have a per capita competitive advantage, it has a dispersal advantage. Once it is everywhere from Ottawa to Tena it becomes a high-frequency, high m component of the American metacommunity.

In a zero sum community J is fixed. The invader can only be accommodated by random replacement of individuals of resident species. The expected absolute number of resident individuals replaced is proportional to local standing richness and to the invader’s metacommunity relative abundance. That means the same neutral increase in frequency of a ubiquitous taxon removes more native species in absolute terms where α is initially large and removes less where α is initially small.

Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado start with a large local species pool and are close to the neutral saturation curve for their J and m. Ottawa, State College, Charlotte start with a small pool and are far from saturation. The pan-American propagule rain therefore raises the effective immigration rescue at the high latitude, low-m end disproportionately and acts as a homogenising flux along the transect. Beta diversity falls as the same common neutral element is sampled at essentially the same frequency everywhere.

That is the classic neutral homogenisation effect: a widespread common species raises the floor of alpha diversity more than the ceiling. In absolute terms the tropical sites have more species to lose to drift and the invader’s rise to high relative abundance via drift will stochastically exclude rare natives there, while the temperate sites are “filled in” by the increased connectivity. The rank order is preserved initially but the tropical temperate contrast is eroded.

Formally the proportional gain is ΔSα/Sα ≈ c/Sα, so the relative increase is largest in the species poor north. The parallel shift argument requires the invader to be added without displacement and with a latitude independent occupancy. That is inconsistent with zero sum sampling. In Hubbell the latitudinal alpha gradient is a neutral speciation-dispersal-drift gradient, not a gradient in per capita competitive ability.

Local equilibrium richness is

E[Sα | J,m,θ] ≈ θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)] ,    θ = 2Jmν

with J the local community size, m the per capita immigration probability and ν the per lineage speciation rate. The metacommunity θ, and in the usual geographical implementation ν, is larger towards the equator, so that

Sα(λ)≈f[J,m(λ),θ(λ)]

is higher towards the equator because the regional species pool and the rescue effect of immigration are larger there. Species identity and species specific competitive superiority are not parameters of the model.

In the neutral limit the European insect is just another ecologically equivalent lineage. Per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical for the invader and for the natives, so the putative “potential to out-compete’’ is null. The invader can only change local composition by neutral drift and by the propagule flux it now supplies to the American metacommunity.

Once the invader is pan-American it is incorporated into the regional abundance distribution on neutral terms. In expectation it is present at every site that is connected to the metacommunity and it is sampled locally in proportion to its metacommunity relative abundance. In the additive approximation

Sα,i(t→∞) ≈ Sα,i^0 + p_occ ,     p_occ≈ x̂_inv ,

with p_occ essentially latitude independent because the invader is assumed to reach every site. In absolute units the species-latitude curve is therefore translated up in parallel,

Sα,post(λ)≈Sα,pre(λ)+const ,

so that ΔSα,tropics-north and dSα/d lat are conserved. There is no neutrally generated, latitudinally biased loss of native α. A systematic, competition driven erosion of tropical richness and a steepening/flattening of the gradient produced by directional exclusion is a niche prediction and is absent under exact neutrality.

The only neutral effect of a truly cosmopolitan, high-m taxon is the familiar neutral homogenisation. Immigration limitation is strongest at the high-latitude, species-poor end of the transect, so the fractional increase ΔSα/Sα is larger in the north than in the already saturated tropics. In proportional terms d ln Sα/d lat is therefore weakly attenuated and β-diversity falls, i.e. the gradient looks a little less steep in relative units. That is a dispersal-drift homogenisation effect, not a niche competitive displacement of tropical natives, and in the strict zero-sum formulation the total individuals J is held constant so the invasive is accommodated by random neutral replacement. In absolute, competition relevant terms the equatorward increase in site level α-diversity persists and the latitudinal α-diversity slope is essentially maintained by the underlying neutral geography of θ,m,ν. The competition driven tropical loss that motivated the re-visit has no neutral counterpart.
public_text.1:
Under the UNTB the 12 sites are samples from a latitudinally structured metacommunity in which all species in the trophic level are ecologically equivalent. Per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical for all lineages so that the per capita competitive superiority invoked in niche theory is null by construction. 

Local alpha richness is therefore a neutral sampling outcome

$S_{\alpha}\simeq f[J,m,\theta],\qquad \theta=2J_{m}\nu$,

set by local community size $J$, immigration $m$ and the fundamental biodiversity number $\theta$ of the metacommunity that feeds the site. The present equator-to-pole increase in $S_{\alpha}$

$S_{\alpha}(\lambda)\approx\theta(\lambda)\,[{\rm \psi}(J+\theta(\lambda))-{\rm \psi}(\theta(\lambda))]$

is the neutral speciation–drift–dispersal gradient, essentially a latitudinally varying $\nu(\lambda)$ and metacommunity size, not a gradient in local competitive ability.

Once the European insect is everywhere from Tena to Ottawa it is in the neutral limit just one more ecologically equivalent neutral lineage now part of the American metacommunity. It cannot systematically drive natives out by niche displacement. In expectation it is incorporated by the same zero-sum multinomial drift-immigration dynamics as any other species and, with the assumed rapid pan-continental dispersal, acquires an occupancy that tends to one at every site.

To first order

$S_{\alpha}^{\rm post}(\lambda)\approx S_{\alpha}^{\rm pre}(\lambda)+\Delta S_{0}$,

i.e. the whole alpha–latitude curve is translated up in parallel by the essentially latitude-independent occupancy of a cosmopolitan neutral taxon. In absolute units

$\Delta S_{\alpha}^{tropics-north}\equiv S_{\alpha}^{tropics}-S_{\alpha}^{temperate}$

and hence $dS_{\alpha}/d{\rm lat}$ set by the latitudinal $\nu/m/J$ gradient is conserved. There is no neutrally predicted, latitude-biased loss of native alpha richness and no niche-style competitive erosion of tropical diversity.

The usual saturating neutral sampling function $\partial S_{\alpha}/\partial\theta>0$, $\partial^{2}S_{\alpha}/\partial\theta^{2}<0$ makes the proportional effect of adding a ubiquitous neutral species larger where $S_{\alpha}$ is initially low. That is the neutral analogue of biotic homogenisation: the proportional slope $d\ln S_{\alpha}/d{\rm lat}$ is weakly attenuated and $\beta$ diversity falls, so the gradient looks slightly flatter in relative terms and the northern sites are lifted toward the regional mean. The flattening is dispersal/drift homogenisation, not a competition-driven tropical loss. The qualitative equatorward increase in site level alpha diversity, the neutral speciation–drift gradient, persists and the competitive exclusion story has no neutral counterpart.

Under strict UNTB a species is a species and a competitor is a competitor only in the niche language.  Per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical for the European insect and for any native it shares a trophic level with, so the “potential to out compete” is operationally null.  Local alpha is

E[Sα| J,m,θ] ≈ θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)] ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] ,

θ =2 Jm ν

a neutral sampling outcome of a metacommunity whose size and per line age speciation rate ν are geographically structured.  The equatorward increase in Sα that you see now,

Sα(λ)≈ f[J,m(λ),θ(λ)] ,

is therefore the neutral speciation – immigration – drift gradient, i.e. a larger regional γ and a larger θ towards the low latitudes, not a local competitive filter.

A truly pan-American, highly dispersive lineage is in the neutral limit just one more ecologically equivalent draw into the American metacommunity.  On the demographic time scale it acquires a metacommunity relative abundance \hat xinv and an occupancy that tends to one over the 12 sites and it is incorporated into each local community by the same zero sum multinomial drift/immigration that governs the natives.  To first order

Sα,post(λ) ≈ Sα,pre(λ)+ΔS0 ,   ΔS0≈ \hat xinv ,

i.e. an essentially latitude independent addition to local richness.  In the zero sum formulation the invader replaces individuals at random, so there is no neutrally predictable, latitudinally biased loss of natives. The absolute tropics – temperate difference

ΔSαtrop-north = Sα,trop – Sα,north

and the absolute derivative dSα/dlat set by the latitudinal variation in ν and in the regional θ are therefore conserved. The classic neutral latitudinal diversity gradient is maintained and the competitive exclusion story has no neutral counterpart.

The well known saturating form Sα≈θ ln[1+J/θ] makes the addition look like a weak homogenisation in proportional terms: ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0, so a constant Δθ or a constant ubiquitous occupancy raises the species poor, high latitude sites a larger fraction than the species rich equatorial sites and d ln Sα/dlat is modestly reduced.  Beta diversity falls and the local communities become more similar to the regional mean, i.e. the usual neutral homogenisation/dispersal effect.  That is a dispersal – drift effect and not a niche competitive erosion of tropical alpha.  In absolute units the neutrally generated equatorward increase in site level alpha persists and, to a very good approximation, the Sα–latitude relationship is translated upward in parallel with no systematic competition driven flattening or reversal of the gradient. ∎

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The 12 sites are a classic pole-to-equator alpha gradient. Under Hubbell UNTB all species in the trophic level are ecologically equivalent; per-capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical, so per-capita competitive superiority is null. Local alpha at equilibrium is neutral sampling of the metacommunity: Sα ≈ f(J,m,θ), θ=2Jm ν, with θ, m and J latitudinally varying. The observed increase toward the equator is therefore a neutral speciation-drift-immigration gradient, not niche filtering.

The European invader, once truly pan-American, is in the neutral limit just another ecologically equivalent lineage now part of the American metacommunity. It has no systematic niche advantage; its fate is drift + immigration. In expectation it acquires a metacommunity relative abundance x̂_inv and occupancy →1 at all 12 sites. Zero-sum multinomial: it can only replace individuals at random.

Core neutral null: no latitude-biased competitive loss. In additive bookkeeping the first-order effect is
Sα,post(λ) ≈ Sα,pre(λ)+ΔS0, ΔS0 ≈ p_occ ≈ x̂_inv essentially latitude independent, so the whole Sα vs latitude curve is translated up in parallel. In absolute units ΔSα,tropics-north and dSα/d lat set by ν(λ), m(λ), J are conserved. The classic equatorward increase persists; the niche expectation of a tropical loss by competitive exclusion is null.

Second-order neutral homogenisation: Sα(θ,J) is saturating, ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0. Adding a ubiquitous high-m neutral taxon raises effective connectivity and immigration rescue. The proportional gain ΔSα/Sα is larger where Sα is initially low. Hence d ln Sα/d lat is weakly attenuated, β-diversity falls, local communities converge toward the metacommunity mean. Northern, immigration-limited, species-poor sites Ottawa/State College/Charlotte are lifted proportionally more than saturated equatorial sites Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado. This is dispersal-drift homogenisation, not competitive displacement.

Disagreement persists across the current round:
Maintain/conserve slope in absolute units camp: Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,8 argue the slope is essentially unchanged; at most a parallel upward shift and a trivial proportional flattening due to saturation. Flatten/homogenise camp: Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21,2,3,4,5,7,9 argue the zero-sum replacement is random with respect to identity but not with respect to local richness, so absolute loss in expectation is larger where richness is largest. The ubiquitous invader raises the floor faster than the ceiling, convergence of alpha across the transect, and the fitted alpha-latitude slope declines in magnitude, tending toward flat in the well-mixed m→1 limit.

Unresolved tension: whether strict zero-sum neutrality gives exact slope conservation with a uniform ΔS, or a weak absolute flattening because marginal gain dS/dθ is diminishing and replacement removes more species in absolute terms in the tropics. The proportional vs absolute reporting of the slope matters. Competition-driven tropical erosion is rejected by all under strict neutrality; the only permissible change is neutral homogenisation/dispersal.

Earlier round insight remains: no competitive, latitude-dependent erosion of tropical alpha is predicted under UNTB. The neutral null to be compared against is maintained equatorward increase, with at most neutral biotic homogenisation reducing relative slope.

Mechanistic tension is between formal parallel shift with absolute slope conserved and a neutral dispersal homogenisation that weakens the gradient in proportional/variance terms and, under strict zero-sum replacement, can be argued to erode the absolute slope.

Because Sα(θ) is concave, the marginal neutral gain from a continent-wide propagule rain is largest where Sα is initially low and immigration limitation is strong, i.e. Ottawa/State College/Charlotte/Merida, and smallest where Sα is near neutral saturation, i.e. Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado. reflection_text.1:
The UNTB null remains decisive: per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical for all species in the trophic level, so per capita competitive superiority is null by construction. Local alpha richness is a neutral sampling outcome Sα≈f[J,m,θ], θ=2Jmν, set by local J, immigration m and the fundamental biodiversity number θ of the metacommunity that feeds the site. The observed equator-to-pole increase in Sα is under neutrality a speciation/drift/dispersal gradient, essentially a latitudinally varying ν and metacommunity size, not niche filtering.

The European insect, once it reaches every site from Tena to Ottawa, is in the neutral limit just one more ecologically equivalent neutral lineage now part of the American metacommunity. It cannot systematically drive natives out by niche displacement. In expectation it is incorporated by the same zero-sum multinomial drift-immigration dynamics as any other species, with occupancy tending to one because of assumed rapid pan-continental dispersal.

That gives the neutral null to the niche competitive-exclusion story. To first order colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4,6,8 argue Sαpost(λ)≈Sαpre(λ)+ΔS0, i.e. the whole α–latitude curve is translated up in parallel by an essentially latitude-independent occupancy of a cosmopolitan neutral taxon. In absolute units ΔSαtropics-north and dSα/dlat set by the latitudinal ν/m/J gradient are conserved, no neutrally predicted latitude-biased loss of native alpha richness occurs, and the qualitative equatorward increase persists.

The debate in round 1 is how that constant addition is expressed under zero-sum sampling. Sα(θ,J) is saturating, ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0. Adding a ubiquitous species therefore raises Sα proportionally more where Sα is initially low, i.e. at high-latitude immigration-limited sites, and relatively less at species-saturated equatorial sites. Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21,2,5,7 describe this as neutral homogenisation / biotic homogenisation: β diversity falls, the α gradient is damped and in relative/proportional terms d ln Sα/dlat looks flatter, tending toward the metacommunity mean under strong mixing, with an absolute flattening if zero-sum replacement is strictly enforced because the same neutral increase removes more species in absolute terms where standing richness is largest.

Colleagues 1,10,12,19,20,18,8 argue the core neutral statement is slope conservation in absolute units; any flattening is a second-order dispersal-homogenisation effect, not a competition-driven tropical loss, and the qualitative equatorward increase persists as the neutral speciation-drift gradient. Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21 argue the saturating, zero-sum nature makes the effect more than proportional: northern sites are lifted toward the regional mean, tropical excess diluted, and the fitted dSα/dlat declines in magnitude with time, tending to a flatter dispersal-dominated pattern.

Unresolved nuance: whether to report the effect as strictly conserved absolute slope with a parallel upward shift, versus the practically often-quoted slight neutral homogenisation/flattening in proportional terms due to saturating richness and increased effective m from a pan-American source, and whether zero-sum strictly implies an absolute erosion of the tropical-temperate contrast. The competition-driven, latitude-dependent erosion of tropical diversity predicted by niche theory is neutrally absent, which is the main point the question targets.

I retain the latitudinal ν,m,J drivers, ecological equivalence, zero-sum neutral sampling, and the distinction between absolute slope conservation and relative homogenisation as the persistent tension in the deliberation.

reflection_text.20:
The question is the long-term latitudinal slope of site-level alpha diversity under Hubbell UNTB after a European insect becomes pan-American.

Core neutral premises shared:
* UNTB: per capita birth, death, immigration, speciation identical for all species; no niche competitive superiority. Species identity irrelevant.
* Local alpha Sα≈f[J,m,θ] with θ=2Jmν, the fundamental biodiversity number. Present latitudinal increase in Sα is a neutral speciation/dispersal/drift gradient, not local competition.

Maintained / essentially parallel shift camp – Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,6,8
* Long term equilibrium: invader acquires metacommunity relative abundance x̂_inv and occupancy→1. To first order Sα,post(λ)≈Sα,pre(λ)+ΔS0 with ΔS0 essentially latitude independent. * Zero-sum: invader replaces individuals at random; no latitudinally biased loss of natives. Competition-driven tropical loss is niche, absent under neutrality.
* Proportional / homogenisation caveat acknowledged: Sα(θ,J) is saturating, ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0. Adding a ubiquitous neutral species raises Sα by larger fraction at species-poor high-latitude sites. Hence d ln Sα/dlat is weakly attenuated, β-diversity falls. Flattening is dispersal/drift homogenisation, not competitive displacement. In strict absolute terms slope is maintained.

Flatten/homogenise camp – Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,21,3,4,5,7,9
* A pan-American high-dispersal invader raises effective connectivity/m everywhere and becomes a high-frequency neutral element. Immigration limitation is strongest at high latitudes, drift strongest there. Marginal neutral gain dSα/dθ is largest where Sα is low and saturating, so northern sites are lifted toward regional mean proportionally more than saturated equatorial sites.
* In strict zero-sum J fixed, invader is accommodated by neutral replacement. Expected absolute number of natives replaced is larger where standing richness is larger, i.e. tropical sites Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado lose more species in absolute terms than Ottawa/State College/Charlotte gain. Current synthesis:

Core disagreement remains whether that homogenisation is strong enough to flatten the absolute slope or merely weakens relative differences. Unresolved: treatment of J constancy, how m is altered by a ubiquitous disperser, and how to formalise flattening as change in θ(lat) vs sampling variance. The saturating neutral sampling function ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0 gives a second-order proportional homogenisation: a constant ubiquitous species raises Sα by a larger fraction at species-poor high-latitude sites than at saturated equatorial sites, so d ln Sα/dlat is weakly attenuated and β diversity falls. Flatten / homogenise camp, Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,21,3,4,5,7,9: the same equivalence is why the gradient is eroded. Immigration limitation is strongest at Ottawa/State College/Charlotte; Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado are already near neutral saturation. The invader therefore lifts the alpha floor in the north proportionally more than the ceiling in the tropics, and the absolute number of native individuals stochastically replaced is larger where standing richness is larger. The flattening is described as neutral biotic homogenisation, not competitive displacement.

Intermediate nuance repeatedly noted: the additive constant story is the non-interacting bookkeeping limit. ∂Sα/∂θ>0, ∂²Sα/∂θ²<0,   Sα≈θ ln[1+J/θ],

so the marginal neutral gain from an increase in effective connectivity is biggest where Sα is initially low and smallest where Sα is already near saturation.

The northern sites are pushed up toward the regional mean while the equatorial sites experience the invader mostly as neutral replacement of rare natives by drift.

The net neutral expectation is convergence of local communities toward a more similar metacommunity mean: beta diversity falls, the north-south contrast in Sα is eroded, and the fitted Sα vs latitude relationship becomes shallower with time. In rank order the tropics remain richer, but the increase per degree latitude, dSα/dlat, declines in magnitude. In the idealised well-mixed neutral limit the gradient is erased toward a common dispersal-dominated expectation.

That is the classic neutral homogenisation prediction, not a niche competitive loss. The invasion is neutrally neutral in the sense of no per capita competitive advantage, but it is not neutrally inert for the observed slope: pan-continental dispersal raises effective m everywhere, drift is strongest where communities are small and immigration limited, and the saturating neutral species–area/immigration curve makes the alpha-latitude contrast converge. and $dS_{\alpha}/d{\rm lat}>0$ set by the latitudinal $\nu,m,J$ gradient is conserved. The latitudinal alpha gradient we see now is a neutral speciation–immigration–drift gradient, Sα≈θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)] with θ=2Jmν, and the tropics are higher because θ(λ), m(λ) and effectively J(λ) are larger toward the equator. That part is neutral and is what Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20 are describing.

Where the parallel-shift story breaks down is zero-sum sampling. Once the European lineage is truly pan-American it is not an additive species, it is a high-frequency, high-m neutral particle that is now part of the American metacommunity. With fixed local J it can only be accommodated by neutral replacement in the multinomial lottery. The expected local richness is saturating in the metacommunity parameter,

∂Sα/∂θ>0, ∂²Sα/∂θ²<0,   Sα≈θ ln[1+J/θ],

so the marginal neutral gain from an increase in effective connectivity is biggest where Sα is initially low and smallest where Sα is already near saturation.

That is exactly the geometry of the 12 sites. Ottawa, State College, Charlotte are immigration limited and far from the neutral saturation curve set by their J and m. Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui are already close to the high-θ, high-m end of the curve and sit on a much larger standing pool of rare species. A continent-wide propagule rain from a ubiquitous neutral taxon therefore lifts the floor of alpha in the north proportionally far more than it lifts the ceiling in the tropics, and in zero-sum terms it stochastically replaces more native individuals in absolute terms where the pool is largest.

Colleague 1,10,11 already concede this as proportional homogenisation: d ln Sα/dlat is weakly attenuated and β-diversity falls because the saturating sampling function makes ΔSα/Sα larger at species-poor high latitude sites. That proportional statement is not separable from absolute change in this setting. With a saturating Sα(θ), an essentially latitude-independent increase in effective θ/m from a cosmopolitan element produces a latitude-dependent absolute increment ΔSα(λ). The northern sites are pushed up toward the regional mean while the equatorial sites experience the invader mostly as neutral replacement of rare natives by drift.

The net neutral expectation is convergence of local communities toward a more similar metacommunity mean: beta diversity falls, the north-south contrast in Sα is eroded, and the fitted Sα vs latitude relationship becomes shallower with time. In rank order the tropics remain richer, but the increase per degree latitude, dSα/dlat, declines in magnitude. In the idealised well-mixed neutral limit the gradient is erased toward a common dispersal-dominated expectation.

That is the classic neutral homogenisation prediction, not a niche competitive loss. The invasion is neutrally neutral in the sense of no per capita competitive advantage, but it is not neutrally inert for the observed slope: pan-continental dispersal raises effective m everywhere, drift is strongest where communities are small and immigration limited, and the saturating neutral species–area/immigration curve makes the alpha-latitude contrast converge. The absolute slope set by θ(λ) is therefore progressively dampened and flattens relative to the pre-invasion baseline.

Implications for the invader: in strict neutrality the European insect has no intrinsic competitive advantage. With pan-American dispersal it becomes a ubiquitous high-frequency immigrant, incorporated by the same zero-sum multinomial drift-immigration dynamics. To first order Sα,post(λ)≈Sα,pre(λ)+ΔS0 with ΔS0 essentially latitude independent, i.e. a parallel upward shift of the alpha-vs-latitude curve. The ongoing disagreement is how the saturating neutral sampling function matters. Sα≈θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)]≈θ ln[1+J/θ] is concave: ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0. Adding a ubiquitous neutral taxon raises effective connectivity/m and β diversity falls. The UNTB null remains the anchor: per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical for all species in the trophic level, so per capita competitive superiority is null by construction. Local alpha richness is a neutral sampling outcome Sα≈E[S|J,m,θ]≈θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)]≈θ ln[1+J/θ], θ=2Jmν, set by local J, immigration m and the fundamental biodiversity number θ of the metacommunity that feeds the site. The European insect, once it reaches every site from Tena to Ottawa, is in the neutral limit just one more ecologically equivalent neutral lineage now part of the American metacommunity. It cannot systematically drive natives out by niche displacement. In expectation it is incorporated by the same zero-sum multinomial drift-immigration dynamics as any other species, with occupancy tending to one because of assumed rapid pan-continental dispersal.

The competition-driven, latitude-dependent erosion of tropical diversity predicted by niche theory is neutrally absent, which is the main point the question targets.

I retain the latitudinal ν,m,J drivers, ecological equivalence, zero-sum neutral sampling, and the distinction between absolute slope conservation and relative homogenisation as the persistent tension in the deliberation.

reflection_text.20:

Core neutral premises persist and are shared:

Earlier points about no competitive superiority and neutral null remain important.

The proportional gain ΔSα/Sα is larger where Sα is initially low. Hence d ln Sα/d lat is weakly attenuated, β-diversity falls, local communities converge toward the metacommunity mean. Northern immigration-limited, species-poor sites Ottawa/State College/Charlotte are lifted proportionally more than saturated equatorial sites Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado. No one defends a competition-driven tropical erosion under strict neutrality; the only permissible change is neutral homogenisation/dispersal. With strict zero-sum J fixed the invader is accommodated by neutral replacement, not free addition. A continent-wide propagule rain raises effective connectivity/m everywhere, essentially a latitude-independent increase in effective θ/m. Because Sα(θ,J) is concave the marginal neutral gain dSα/dθ is diminishing. With ecological equivalence birth, death, immigration and speciation are per capita identical. Local alpha is the neutral sampling expectation

E[Sα|J,m,θ]≈θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)]≈θ ln[1+J/θ],  θ=2Jmν

a saturating concave function of θ and effective immigration m. The present Tena→Ottawa increase is the neutral speciation-drift-immigration gradient: θ(λ), m(λ) and ν(λ) are larger toward the equator so Sα is larger in the tropics and smaller and immigration limited in the north. That is agreed.

What changes once the European lineage is truly pan-American is effective connectivity. With rapid range-wide dispersal it is now a high-frequency, m≈1 component of the American metacommunity of the guild. In the zero-sum multinomial J is fixed, so it is accommodated by neutral replacement, not by free addition of individuals.

Because ∂Sα/∂θ>0 and ∂²Sα/∂θ²<0 the marginal neutral gain from an increase in effective θ/m is diminishing. The sites at the high-latitude end of the transect – Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Merida – are far from neutral saturation for their J and are immigration limited. The equatorial sites – Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui – are already close to the saturation set by a large tropical θ and high effective m.

A continent-wide propagule rain therefore raises expected richness in proportional terms much more at the species-poor north than at the species-saturated tropics. In absolute terms the increment ΔSα(λ) is latitude dependent. If effective θ/m is raised essentially uniformly, Δθ≈const,

[Sα(θ_trop+Δθ)-Sα(θ_north+Δθ)] < [Sα(θ_trop)-Sα(θ_north)]

because of concavity. The floor is lifted toward the regional mean while the ceiling moves little; the same ubiquitous neutral taxon is accommodated in the tropics mainly by stochastic replacement of the large standing pool of rare natives.

That is classic neutral drift-immigration homogenisation. β-diversity falls as the same cosmopolitan element is now shared from Tena to Ottawa and local communities converge toward a more similar metacommunity mean. The rank order equatorward>poleward is retained for a while because ν(λ) is still latitudinally varying, but the empirical fitted increase in species per degree latitude, dSα/dlat, is progressively dampened and the tropical-temperate contrast Sα,tropics–Sα,north is eroded with time. In the idealised well-mixed neutral limit the gradient is erased toward a dispersal-dominated common expectation.

The Sαpost≈Sαpre+ΔS0 parallel-shift with ΔS0 latitude independent is the additive bookkeeping limit with J allowed to increase. With strict zero-sum sampling the effect of a ubiquitous high-m neutral species is not latitude independent in its impact on richness; it is greatest where communities are small/immigration limited and smallest where they are near saturation. The UNTB null remains the anchor: per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical for all species in the trophic level, so per capita competitive superiority is null by construction. Local alpha richness is a neutral sampling outcome Sα≈E[S|J,m,θ]≈θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)]≈θ ln[1+J/θ], θ=2Jmν, set by local J, immigration m and the fundamental biodiversity number θ of the metacommunity that feeds the site. The observed equator-to-pole increase Sα(λ) is under neutrality a speciation/drift/dispersal gradient, essentially a latitudinally varying ν(λ), m(λ), J(λ) and metacommunity size, not niche filtering.

The European insect, once it reaches every site from Tena to Ottawa, is in the neutral limit just one more ecologically equivalent neutral lineage now part of the American metacommunity. It cannot systematically drive natives out by niche displacement. In expectation it is incorporated by the same zero-sum multinomial drift-immigration dynamics as any other species, with occupancy tending to one because of assumed rapid pan-continental dispersal.

That gives the neutral null to the niche competitive-exclusion story. To first order colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4,6,8 argue Sαpost(λ)≈Sαpre(λ)+ΔS0, i.e. the whole α–latitude curve is translated up in parallel by an essentially latitude-independent occupancy of a cosmopolitan neutral taxon. In absolute units ΔSαtropics-north and dSα/dlat set by the latitudinal ν/m/J gradient are conserved, no neutrally predicted latitude-biased loss of native alpha richness occurs, and the qualitative equatorward increase persists.

The debate in round 2-3 is how that constant addition is expressed under zero-sum sampling. Sα(θ,J) is saturating, ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0. Adding a ubiquitous species therefore raises Sα proportionally more where Sα is initially low, i.e. at high-latitude immigration-limited sites, and relatively less at species-saturated equatorial sites. Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21,2,5,7 describe this as neutral homogenisation / biotic homogenisation: β diversity falls, the α gradient is damped and in relative/proportional terms d ln Sα/dlat looks flatter, tending toward the metacommunity mean under strong mixing, with an absolute flattening if zero-sum replacement is strictly enforced because the same neutral increase removes more species in absolute terms where standing richness is largest.

Colleagues 1,10,12,19,20,18,8 argue the core neutral statement is slope conservation in absolute units; any flattening is a second-order dispersal-homogenisation effect, not a competition-driven tropical loss, and the qualitative equatorward increase persists as the neutral speciation-drift gradient. Unresolved nuance: whether to report the effect as strictly conserved absolute slope with a parallel upward shift, versus the practically often-quoted slight neutral homogenisation/flattening in proportional terms due to saturating richness and increased effective m from a pan-American source, and whether zero-sum strictly implies an absolute erosion of the tropical-temperate contrast. The competition-driven, latitude-dependent erosion of tropical diversity predicted by niche theory is neutrally absent, which is the main point the question targets.

I retain the latitudinal ν,m,J drivers, ecological equivalence, zero-sum neutral sampling, and the distinction between absolute slope conservation and relative homogenisation as the persistent tension in the deliberation.

* Distinction between absolute slope conservation vs proportional flattening. Many colleagues acknowledge weak proportional homogenisation even while claiming absolute conservation.
* How to formalise “flattening” as change in θ(lat) vs change in sampling variance/drift. No consensus on quantitative magnitude.

Current synthesis:
Under strict neutrality there is no competition-driven tropical loss; the latitudinal alpha gradient is the neutral speciation/drift gradient. The neutral null is at best a parallel upward shift with conserved absolute dSα/dlat and at most a mild dispersal-mediated homogenisation that attenuates the proportional slope d ln Sα/dlat. Core disagreement remains whether that homogenisation is strong enough to flatten the absolute slope or merely weakens relative differences. Unresolved: treatment of J constancy, how m is altered by a ubiquitous disperser, and how to formalise flattening as change in θ(lat) vs sampling variance. Earlier points about no competitive superiority and neutral null remain important.

reflection_text.1:
The UNTB null remains the anchor for the deliberation: per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are identical for all species in the trophic level, so per capita competitive superiority is null by construction. Local alpha richness is a neutral sampling outcome

E[Sα|J,m,θ] ≃ θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)] ≃ θ ln[1+J/θ],  θ=2Jmν,

set by local J, immigration m and the fundamental biodiversity number θ of the metacommunity that feeds the site. The observed equator-to-pole increase Sα(λ) is under neutrality a speciation/drift/dispersal gradient, essentially a latitudinally varying ν(λ), m(λ), J(λ) and metacommunity size, not niche filtering.

The European insect, once it reaches every site from Tena to Ottawa, is in the neutral limit just one more ecologically equivalent neutral lineage now part of the American metacommunity. It cannot systematically drive natives out by niche displacement. In expectation it is incorporated by the same zero-sum multinomial drift-immigration dynamics as any other species, with occupancy tending to one because of assumed rapid pan-continental dispersal.

That gives the neutral null to the niche competitive-exclusion story. To first order colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4,6,8 argue Sαpost(λ)≈Sαpre(λ)+ΔS0, i.e. the whole α–latitude curve is translated up in parallel by an essentially latitude-independent occupancy of a cosmopolitan neutral taxon. In absolute units ΔSαtropics-north and dSα/dlat set by the latitudinal ν/m/J gradient are conserved, no neutrally predicted latitude-biased loss of native alpha richness occurs, and the qualitative equatorward increase persists.

The debate in round 2-3 is how that constant addition is expressed under zero-sum sampling. Sα(θ,J) is saturating, ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0. Adding a ubiquitous species therefore raises Sα proportionally more where Sα is initially low, i.e. at high-latitude immigration-limited sites, and relatively less at species-saturated equatorial sites. Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21,2,5,7 describe this as neutral homogenisation / biotic homogenisation: β diversity falls, the α gradient is damped and in relative/proportional terms d ln Sα/dlat looks flatter, tending toward the metacommunity mean under strong mixing, with an absolute flattening if zero-sum replacement is strictly enforced because the same neutral increase removes more species in absolute terms where standing richness is largest.

Colleagues 1,10,12,19,20,18,8 argue the core neutral statement is slope conservation in absolute units; any flattening is a second-order dispersal-homogenisation effect, not a competition-driven tropical loss, and the qualitative equatorward increase persists as the neutral speciation-drift gradient. Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21 argue the saturating, zero-sum nature makes the effect more than proportional: northern sites are lifted toward the regional mean, tropical excess diluted, and the fitted dSα/dlat declines in magnitude with time, tending to a flatter dispersal-dominated pattern, with in the idealised m→1 limit slope→0.

Unresolved nuance: whether to report the effect as strictly conserved absolute slope with a parallel upward shift, versus the practically often-quoted slight neutral homogenisation/flattening in proportional terms due to saturating richness and increased effective m from a pan-American source, and whether zero-sum strictly implies an absolute erosion of the tropical-temperate contrast. The competition-driven, latitude-dependent erosion of tropical diversity predicted by niche theory is neutrally absent, which is the main point the question targets.

I retain the latitudinal ν,m,J drivers, ecological equivalence, zero-sum neutral sampling, and the distinction between absolute slope conservation and relative homogenisation as the persistent tension in the deliberation.

reflection_text.20:
The question is long-term latitudinal slope of site-level alpha under Hubbell UNTB after a European insect becomes pan-American.

Core neutral premises remain stable and shared:
* UNTB: per capita birth, death, immigration, speciation identical for all species; no niche competitive superiority. Species identity irrelevant.
* Local alpha Sα≈f[J,m,θ] with θ=2Jmν, the fundamental biodiversity number. Present latitudinal increase in Sα is neutral speciation/dispersal/drift geography, not local competition.
* Invader is just another neutrally equivalent lineage in the American metacommunity. Its fate is drift + immigration, not deterministic out-competition.

Round 4 public responses keep two camps with sharpened quantitative arguments.

Parallel-shift / essentially conserved absolute slope camp – 1,11,12,15,20,8,19

* In absolute species per degree latitude ΔSαtropics-north and dSα/dlat set by latitudinal ν(λ),m(λ),J(λ) are conserved. No neutrally generated latitude-biased loss of natives.
* Saturating Sα(θ,J) gives ∂S/∂θ>0, ∂²S/∂θ²<0 so addition of a ubiquitous neutral taxon raises Sα proportionally more where Sα is low. Hence d ln Sα/dlat is weakly attenuated, β-diversity falls, but absolute slope is maintained; this is second-order proportional homogenisation, not competitive displacement.

Flatten / homogenise absolute slope camp – 10,13,14,16,17,2,21,3,4,5,7,9
* Strict zero-sum J fixed. Incorporation of a pan-American high-m lineage occurs by random neutral replacement, not free addition.
* Concavity of Sα(θ,J) is geographically loaded: Ottawa/State College/Charlotte/Merida/Belmopan immigration limited, far from neutral saturation for their J; Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado/Sarapiqui close to high-θ saturation.
* An essentially latitude-independent increase in effective θ/m from a ubiquitous disperser gives latitude-dependent absolute increment ΔSα(λ)=Sα(θ+Δθ,J)-Sα(θ,J). Marginal gain dSα/dθ diminishing in θ → ΔSα largest where Sα initially low, smallest where Sα near saturation.
* In zero-sum terms same metacommunity frequency x̂inv is accommodated by larger absolute number of stochastic replacements where standing pool of rare species is largest, i.e. tropics, while northern floor is lifted toward regional mean. Hence Sα(θtrop+Δθ)-Sα(θnorth+Δθ) < Sα(θtrop)-Sα(θnorth). Tropical-temperate contrast erodes, fitted increase in raw species per degree latitude dampens, slope flattens toward dispersal-dominated common expectation. Points of tension / unresolved persist:
* Zero-sum vs non-zero-sum formulation. Additive constant ΔS0 gives conserved absolute slope; strict zero-sum with saturating sampling function gives latitude-dependent effective gain and argument for absolute erosion.
* Whether invasion effectively increases m everywhere or just adds +1 to regional species pool θ. If m↑ uniformly, Sα(θ) saturates and homogenisation is asymmetric.

Earlier points about no competitive superiority and neutral null remain important.
